# API reference

<!-- Generated by go run ./internal/apidocs/cmd/genapidocs from proto/orkstack/v1. Do not edit. -->

OrkStack's API is a set of [Connect](https://connectrpc.com) services served
by `ork` on one h2c port (`:8080` by default), the same contract
`orkctl` and the UI use ([UI_CLI_PARITY.md](./UI_CLI_PARITY.md)). This page
is generated from the proto sources' own comments: every service, and every
message and enum a service's methods take or return.

A method is called at `/orkstack.v1.<Service>/<Method>`, for example
`POST /orkstack.v1.RunService/SubmitRun`. In JSON a field is spelled in
lowerCamelCase (`task_runs` arrives as `taskRuns`), and enums use the dialect
[JSON.md](./JSON.md) describes. A comment may name an engine-internal message
(such as `ExecuteTaskInput`) that no method carries; it is not part of
the API and is not listed here. OrkStack does not authenticate callers; the
deployment's gateway does, and may assert a principal in `Ork-Principal`
([ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)).

## Services

### ActivityService

ActivityService reports what this deployment can run: an activity is an
image, and which images exist is engine configuration (§4.2), not something
to ask an Orker.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/activity_service.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ListActivities` | [`ListActivitiesRequest`](#listactivitiesrequest) | [`ListActivitiesResponse`](#listactivitiesresponse) |  |
| `DescribeOrker` | [`DescribeOrkerRequest`](#describeorkerrequest) | [`DescribeOrkerResponse`](#describeorkerresponse) | DescribeOrker is the pool-liveness probe (§6.5). It is answered by an Orker of that pool, so it answers only when an Orker is actually polling that pool. |
| `ListOrkers` | [`ListOrkersRequest`](#listorkersrequest) | [`ListOrkersResponse`](#listorkersresponse) | ListOrkers is the fleet: one row per live Orker of the deployment, derived on read. Like Pool, nothing WRITES an Orker — the list comes from the cluster's own poller records and each Orker's own answer, so any replica answers and none holds state of its own (AGENTS.md §7). It NARROWS rather than refusing: an Orker that did not answer keeps its row and carries unavailable_reason. Two conditions are distinct: a known poller whose describe failed is a row with unavailable_reason; an orker_id that NO live poller answers to is an EMPTY list, never NOT_FOUND — a read for an id nothing polls is an empty answer, and the drain loop relies on it (CordonOrker, a write, is the one that answers NOT_FOUND for that id).<br><br>An orker_id EQUALS filter asks exactly that one Orker, and no other, and returns at most one row: it is what `orkctl orker get` and the drain loop send, so a drain costs one activity per poll and not one per Orker of the fleet. Every other filter is applied to the inventory; an unreachable row is kept under a pool, build_id or cordoned filter, since none of those was measured on it. A malformed orker_id in an equals, not-equals or in filter is INVALID_ARGUMENT before any read. |
| `CordonOrker` | [`CordonOrkerRequest`](#cordonorkerrequest) | [`CordonOrkerResponse`](#cordonorkerresponse) | CordonOrker sets or clears ONE Orker's cordon: a process-local flag delivered to that Orker alone, lost when the process exits. A cordoned Orker takes no new task and opens no new pin; everything already in flight on it is untouched. The response is the Orker's state AFTER the change, as the Orker itself reported it. |
| `InspectActivity` | [`InspectActivityRequest`](#inspectactivityrequest) | [`InspectActivityResponse`](#inspectactivityresponse) | InspectActivity resolves ONE reference on demand — a catalog name or any registry reference `uses:` would accept — and reports it as ListActivities would: the pinned digest, platforms, and the interface the image declares. It is uncached, reads engine configuration and the registry only, never asks an Orker, and writes nothing. |

### AuditService

AuditService reads back the control-plane audit trail: one immutable record
per call of a write RPC, written by the engine at the moment the handler
returned, into the shared store (metadata/audit/…), so any replica answers
for a write another replica performed (AGENTS.md §7).

It is a record, never a read path: nothing in OrkStack consults an audit
record to make a decision, so the trail cannot become a second source of
truth about anything (AGENTS.md §2.2). Reads are never recorded; this RPC
is itself a read.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/audit.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ListAuditRecords` | [`ListAuditRecordsRequest`](#listauditrecordsrequest) | [`ListAuditRecordsResponse`](#listauditrecordsresponse) | ListAuditRecords returns records newest first, bounded and paginated.<br><br>A scan that would examine more objects than the engine's budget allows before filling a page is REFUSED (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) naming the budget, never answered from the subset it managed to read: a partial audit listing that looks complete is worse than none. |

### AutomationService

AutomationService plans and exports a namespace's automation document:
its settings, schedules, triggers and webhooks, declared by name
(docs/AUTOMATION.md).

It WRITES NOTHING, ever. PlanAutomation is to an automation document what
ValidateOrkflow is to an orkflow document: the whole preparation an apply
needs, and no write. An apply is performed by the CLIENT, which sends each
actionable step's carried request to the existing RPC it names, in order,
so every write is the same validated, audited call a person could make by
hand. Nothing in the engine applies a document, stores one, or watches for
drift.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/automation.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PlanAutomation` | [`PlanAutomationRequest`](#planautomationrequest) | [`PlanAutomationResponse`](#planautomationresponse) | PlanAutomation parses the document, reads what its namespace holds, and answers with every step an apply would take and every object it would leave alone. Problems with the document are ISSUES, never RPC errors; an unreachable store or cluster is an RPC error, never an empty plan. |
| `ExportAutomation` | [`ExportAutomationRequest`](#exportautomationrequest) | [`ExportAutomationResponse`](#exportautomationresponse) | ExportAutomation renders the document a namespace's current automation would be applied from. Deterministic: the same state exports the same bytes. It refuses rather than omit: an object it cannot read, or two objects sharing a name, fail the export, because an export missing an object would delete it when applied with --prune. |

### CacheService

CacheService reads and trims the memos cached tasks reuse (docs/DSL.md
"Caching"). Memos are advisory: nothing here can change a result, and
PurgeCache only makes the next run of a cached task run its container.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/cache.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetCacheStats` | [`GetCacheStatsRequest`](#getcachestatsrequest) | [`GetCacheStatsResponse`](#getcachestatsresponse) | GetCacheStats reports one namespace's memo inventory, as the store lists it now, and how its cached tasks fared over one window of finished runs, derived on read from the run archive. Nothing is counted or stored. |
| `PurgeCache` | [`PurgeCacheRequest`](#purgecacherequest) | [`PurgeCacheResponse`](#purgecacheresponse) | PurgeCache deletes memos. It never touches a commit, run, attempt, log or artifact. |

### NamespaceService

NamespaceService manages namespaces and reports the pools they may dispatch
onto.

A namespace is a scope that owns orkflow names, runs and pool defaults. The
registry is durable (the artifact store), so any replica answers for any
namespace, including one it never created.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/namespace_service.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateNamespace` | [`CreateNamespaceRequest`](#createnamespacerequest) | [`CreateNamespaceResponse`](#createnamespaceresponse) | CreateNamespace registers a namespace.<br><br>It is idempotent for an identical spec: creating the same namespace twice with the same description, labels, default pool and allowed pools returns the existing document rather than an error, so a provisioning script is safe to re-run. A second create that differs is AlreadyExists, naming what differs — that one is a collision, not a repeat. |
| `GetNamespace` | [`GetNamespaceRequest`](#getnamespacerequest) | [`GetNamespaceResponse`](#getnamespaceresponse) | GetNamespace reads one namespace. The default namespace always resolves, whether or not anyone created it. |
| `ListNamespaces` | [`ListNamespacesRequest`](#listnamespacesrequest) | [`ListNamespacesResponse`](#listnamespacesresponse) | ListNamespaces returns the registered namespaces, ordered by name, with the built-in default always among them.<br><br>page_size 0 returns every match in one response; a positive page_size returns one page and a next_page_token. The names come from the registry's key listing, so a page filtered by name alone (or not at all) reads only the documents it holds: a page of 25 out of thousands costs one listing and 25 reads. A filter on any other field reads documents in name order, a batch at a time, until the page is full. |
| `UpdateNamespace` | [`UpdateNamespaceRequest`](#updatenamespacerequest) | [`UpdateNamespaceResponse`](#updatenamespaceresponse) | UpdateNamespace replaces a namespace's mutable fields.<br><br>It is a compare-and-swap on Namespace.etag: the token a read handed back. A stale token is FailedPrecondition, so two operators editing at once cannot silently clobber each other — the loser re-reads and re-applies. |
| `DeleteNamespace` | [`DeleteNamespaceRequest`](#deletenamespacerequest) | [`DeleteNamespaceResponse`](#deletenamespaceresponse) | DeleteNamespace removes a namespace that holds no orkflows.<br><br>It refuses while any orkflow is still stored in it, and says how many: deleting the registry entry would not delete the definitions, so they would survive under a namespace nothing lists. The default namespace is refused unconditionally — every orkflow that names none is in it. |
| `ListPools` | [`ListPoolsRequest`](#listpoolsrequest) | [`ListPoolsResponse`](#listpoolsresponse) | ListPools reports every pool a namespace may dispatch onto, each with the number of Orkers serving it right now.<br><br>The answer is read from the cluster, never from process memory, so any replica answers — including one that started nothing.<br><br>It NARROWS rather than refusing. A source that cannot be reached costs this read what that source knew and nothing else: a pool the cluster did not answer for is still listed, carrying Pool.unavailable_reason instead of a count; an orkflow store that cannot be read narrows the answer to the pools the namespace document itself names. An admin read is opened when something is already wrong, and a refusal hides the healthy pools beside the broken one. |

### OrkflowService

OrkflowService manages orkflow definitions (the compiled DSL).

A version is immutable and a name is unique within a namespace, so the three
coordinates (namespace, name, version) address one document for all time.
What moves is a per-orkflow POINTER: `current` decides which version an
empty version resolves to, and moving it is the only mutation this service
performs on an existing orkflow.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/orkflow_service.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ValidateOrkflow` | [`ValidateOrkflowRequest`](#validateorkflowrequest) | [`ValidateOrkflowResponse`](#validateorkflowresponse) | ValidateOrkflow performs the same non-mutating preparation as apply. |
| `ApplyOrkflow` | [`ApplyOrkflowRequest`](#applyorkflowrequest) | [`ApplyOrkflowResponse`](#applyorkflowresponse) | ApplyOrkflow validates and stores an orkflow from raw DSL YAML.<br><br>It never rewrites a stored version: identical YAML under an existing version is a no-op that writes nothing, and DIFFERENT YAML under an existing version is refused (AlreadyExists). An edit therefore always arrives as a new version — which is what lets a run pinned to a version keep reading the bytes it pinned. |
| `GetOrkflow` | [`GetOrkflowRequest`](#getorkflowrequest) | [`GetOrkflowResponse`](#getorkflowresponse) |  |
| `ListOrkflows` | [`ListOrkflowsRequest`](#listorkflowsrequest) | [`ListOrkflowsResponse`](#listorkflowsresponse) |  |
| `ListOrkflowVersions` | [`ListOrkflowVersionsRequest`](#listorkflowversionsrequest) | [`ListOrkflowVersionsResponse`](#listorkflowversionsresponse) | ListOrkflowVersions lists every stored version of one orkflow, newest applied first, marking the one an empty version resolves to. |
| `SetCurrentOrkflowVersion` | [`SetCurrentOrkflowVersionRequest`](#setcurrentorkflowversionrequest) | [`SetCurrentOrkflowVersionResponse`](#setcurrentorkflowversionresponse) | SetCurrentOrkflowVersion moves the orkflow's current pointer.<br><br>The target must already exist: promoting to an unknown version is NotFound, so a reader can never observe a pointer to a version that is not there. Two replicas promoting at once are arbitrated by the store's compare-and-swap — one value wins, and it is one of the two asked for.<br><br>It compares the target's declared interface with the version a run that names no version executes now, and REFUSES (FailedPrecondition, naming each breaking finding) a BREAKING change unless acknowledge_breaking is set. COMPATIBLE and UNKNOWN changes are never refused. The swap is made only while the pointer still names what the comparison was made against: a promotion that loses that race is FailedPrecondition, never an unchecked move. |
| `DiffOrkflowVersions` | [`DiffOrkflowVersionsRequest`](#difforkflowversionsrequest) | [`DiffOrkflowVersionsResponse`](#difforkflowversionsresponse) | DiffOrkflowVersions renders the unified diff between two versions' source_yaml.<br><br>The diff is computed SERVER-side, deliberately. Two clients read it (the CLI and the UI) and a third will follow; a client-side diff would put a diff dependency in each of them and let their renderings drift, so that `orkctl orkflow diff` and the version page could disagree about what changed. One implementation, golden-tested once, rendered verbatim by every client. |
| `DeleteOrkflow` | [`DeleteOrkflowRequest`](#deleteorkflowrequest) | [`DeleteOrkflowResponse`](#deleteorkflowresponse) | DeleteOrkflow removes all versions of an orkflow from the registry.<br><br>It refuses (FailedPrecondition) if any runs are currently executing or queued for this orkflow, or if runs have completed recently (within the past 24 hours). The check is conservative: an orkflow with any recent activity cannot be deleted. This protects against accidental deletion of an orkflow in active use.<br><br>The operation is NOT reversible: all versions and their metadata are permanently deleted. Runs that pinned the orkflow keep executing — they have the version they started with — but any new run will fail with NotFound. |
| `PlanRun` | [`PlanRunRequest`](#planrunrequest) | [`PlanRunResponse`](#planrunresponse) | PlanRun answers "for this input, which tasks of this definition would run, which would be skipped and why, and in what order" WITHOUT starting anything.<br><br>It is a read in the shape of ValidateOrkflow: it resolves the same definition SubmitRun would (or prepares an unapplied document exactly as ValidateOrkflow does), applies the same declared input defaults, and walks the DAG with the interpreter's own condition evaluator — the same function RunWorkflow calls, not a copy of it. It writes no definition, no pointer, no execution, no idempotency claim, and no event; no run id is minted. There is no flag that makes it submit.<br><br>A plan proves WIRING, never behaviour: a task reported RUNS is a task the interpreter would dispatch, not a task that would succeed. It is also not an admission check — pools, holds, and limits are SubmitRun's questions and are not asked here. |
| `CompareInterfaces` | [`CompareInterfacesRequest`](#compareinterfacesrequest) | [`CompareInterfacesResponse`](#compareinterfacesresponse) | CompareInterfaces classifies how the DECLARED interface of one stored version — its inputs: and its outputs: — changes in another (docs/DSL.md "Which version runs"). It speaks about declarations only: tasks, images, with:, pools and output templates are implementation, and DiffOrkflowVersions reports them. Computed on every call from the two immutable documents, stored nowhere; any replica answers. |
| `ListOrkflowCallers` | [`ListOrkflowCallersRequest`](#listorkflowcallersrequest) | [`ListOrkflowCallersResponse`](#listorkflowcallersresponse) | ListOrkflowCallers lists what, in this namespace, references one orkflow and which version it pins: every composing task of every other orkflow's scanned version, every trigger, and every schedule. It is a scan of the namespace's stored definitions and a read of its triggers and schedules, made per request — there is no caller index — so its cost grows with the namespace, and the response says how much it read. |

### RunService

RunService submits and observes orkflow executions.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/run_service.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SubmitRun` | [`SubmitRunRequest`](#submitrunrequest) | [`SubmitRunResponse`](#submitrunresponse) |  |
| `GetRun` | [`GetRunRequest`](#getrunrequest) | [`GetRunResponse`](#getrunresponse) |  |
| `ListRuns` | [`ListRunsRequest`](#listrunsrequest) | [`ListRunsResponse`](#listrunsresponse) |  |
| `CancelRun` | [`CancelRunRequest`](#cancelrunrequest) | [`CancelRunResponse`](#cancelrunresponse) |  |
| `StreamEvents` | [`StreamEventsRequest`](#streameventsrequest) | stream [`Event`](#event) | StreamEvents server-streams realtime events for a run. from_sequence allows resuming after a disconnect (0 = from start). |
| `StreamTaskLogs` | [`StreamTaskLogsRequest`](#streamtasklogsrequest) | stream [`TaskLogChunk`](#tasklogchunk) | StreamTaskLogs server-streams one task attempt's output: every chunk already written, in order, then each new one as it lands.<br><br>Logs are a SEPARATE stream from Event on purpose. Task output is bytes, and bytes never enter a Temporal payload or the event stream (a run's history is replayed forever, and a chatty task would bloat it forever too). The Orker writes numbered chunks to the artifact store while the task runs; this RPC reads them back from there. EventType gains nothing: EVENT_TYPE_TASK_LOG stays what it always was, a human notice with no task output in it.<br><br>Any replica answers for any run, on the same terms as StreamEvents: the chunks are in the shared store and the task's state comes from the shared cluster, so a replica that started nothing serves a run to completion. |
| `ListRunArtifacts` | [`ListRunArtifactsRequest`](#listrunartifactsrequest) | [`ListRunArtifactsResponse`](#listrunartifactsresponse) |  |
| `ReadArtifact` | [`ReadArtifactRequest`](#readartifactrequest) | stream [`ArtifactChunk`](#artifactchunk) |  |
| `ListTaskAttempts` | [`ListTaskAttemptsRequest`](#listtaskattemptsrequest) | [`ListTaskAttemptsResponse`](#listtaskattemptsresponse) | ListTaskAttempts reads back what every attempt of a task did, including the attempts that lost.<br><br>Temporal owns retries, so a run's snapshot only ever carries a task's FINAL outcome: the error of each earlier attempt is discarded when the next one is scheduled. The Orker writes one immutable TaskAttempt record per attempt (metadata/attempts/…), and this RPC serves them — from the shared store, so any replica answers for any run, on exactly the terms StreamTaskLogs and ListRunArtifacts are on.<br><br>A missing record is REPORTED, never hidden: an attempt number the store has nothing for comes back as ATTEMPT_OUTCOME_UNREPORTED, so a timeline never has a silent hole where an Orker died. There is no stream: a client refetches on the events it already follows. |
| `ResolveAwait` | [`ResolveAwaitRequest`](#resolveawaitrequest) | [`ResolveAwaitResponse`](#resolveawaitresponse) | ResolveAwait completes or rejects an awaited task of a running run. It is a WRITE, addressed inside a namespace exactly as CancelRun is: another namespace's run is NotFound. The values are stored and the resolution is delivered to the run before this returns; the run applies it — a caller that must see the outcome reads the run or follows its events. A repeat of the resolution that already won answers success and delivers nothing. |
| `GetArtifactProvenance` | [`GetArtifactProvenanceRequest`](#getartifactprovenancerequest) | [`GetArtifactProvenanceResponse`](#getartifactprovenanceresponse) | GetArtifactProvenance answers, for ONE recorded artifact, whether its bytes are still in the object store and which archived runs of the calling namespace recorded the same physical object.<br><br>It is a READ of the reverse index the archive already maintains for cleanup refcounting (metadata/index/objects/…, docs/STORAGE.md): a keys-only prefix scan whose keys are the answer, then one body read per referencing run to check its namespace. It writes nothing and creates no key family.<br><br>The artifact is addressed exactly as ReadArtifact addresses it — by the run, task, kind and recorded name — and resolved against the authoritative run. A caller never names an object key or a URI. On the S3 backend an object key embeds its run id, so `references` is the producing run alone; on the local backend identical bytes under one name are one object, so every run that produced them is listed. |
| `InspectRun` | [`InspectRunRequest`](#inspectrunrequest) | [`InspectRunResponse`](#inspectrunresponse) | InspectRun answers "what is this task doing right now" for every in-flight task of ONE live run, from the heartbeat detail the Orker already sends and the cluster already holds for the pending activity.<br><br>It is a READ of Temporal's own describe of the execution — nothing is stored, nothing is projected onto the snapshot, and no event is added. A run that is terminal, or whose execution has left the cluster, answers with run_status and no attempts. There is no stream: a client polls.<br><br>A heartbeat is reported ONLY when it belongs to the attempt that is pending now. Temporal keeps a failed attempt's last detail through the retry backoff and until the next attempt's first beat; that detail is never rendered as the new attempt's progress. |
| `DiffRuns` | [`DiffRunsRequest`](#diffrunsrequest) | [`DiffRunsResponse`](#diffrunsresponse) | DiffRuns compares two runs of ONE namespace field by field: the pinned definition, the input (as a canonical-JSON unified diff), and per task its status, attempt, pool, pin, orker, exit code, error, duration, and the image it was dispatched with and the platform manifest it ran.<br><br>It is a READ over what GetRun, GetOrkflow and ListTaskAttempts already serve, computed on every call and stored nowhere, so there is no comparison record that can disagree with the runs it compares. Both ids resolve inside the request's namespace exactly as GetRun resolves one: a run of another namespace is NotFound. Two runs of different orkflows are compared and flagged (same_orkflow=false), never refused.<br><br>The diff is SERVER-side for the reason DiffOrkflowVersions records: two clients render it, and the rendering of "unavailable", "does not apply" and an empty value must be decided once. Every from_value/to_value is a rendered string a client prints verbatim. |
| `ExportRunEvidence` | [`ExportRunEvidenceRequest`](#exportrunevidencerequest) | stream [`EvidenceChunk`](#evidencechunk) | ExportRunEvidence streams ONE finished run's evidence bundle: a tar.gz whose first member, MANIFEST.json, names every other member's path, origin, size, sha256 and state, followed by the archived run and events, the pinned definition's source YAML, and per task the verbatim commit.json, values.json, every output artifact, every attempt record, and every attempt's stdout.log and stderr.log.<br><br>It is a READ, assembled per request from objects that already exist and kept nowhere: there is no export record, so nothing can disagree with the archive. Every member digest is of the bytes as they were read; a member with a recorded reference is verified as it streams and a mismatch ends the stream with DataLoss and no `last`. Bytes the cleanup worker or a lifecycle rule removed are listed with state "reclaimed" and their recorded sha256 preserved, never omitted.<br><br>The run is addressed inside its namespace exactly as GetRun addresses it and must be finished and archived; a live run is FailedPrecondition. The stream is complete only when a chunk with `last` arrives, on the same terms as ReadArtifact. The bundle layout and manifest schema are docs/RUN_EVIDENCE.md. |

### ScheduleService

ScheduleService manages schedules: objects bound to ONE orkflow in one
namespace that start a run of it whenever a Temporal Schedule fires.

It is the third starter beside SubmitRun and TriggerService, and it starts
runs the way both of them do — through the ordinary submit preparation,
with the version pointer resolved at fire time when none is pinned — so
a scheduled run is an ordinary run with origin.kind = SCHEDULE.

Temporal owns every piece of schedule state (AGENTS.md §2.1). OrkStack
stores NOTHING for a schedule: the coordinates below live inside the
Temporal Schedule itself, and paused, note, next_fire_times and
recent_fires are read from the cluster on every call. There is no
OrkStack column that could disagree with Temporal's.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/schedule.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateSchedule` | [`CreateScheduleRequest`](#createschedulerequest) | [`CreateScheduleResponse`](#createscheduleresponse) | CreateSchedule creates one schedule. The namespace is resolved and the orkflow (and pinned version, when one is given) confirmed to exist before the cluster is asked, on the checks CreateTrigger makes; a refused create creates nothing. A name already in use in the namespace is AlreadyExists. The cluster's own refusal of the spec (a cron expression it cannot parse) is InvalidArgument quoting its message. |
| `ListSchedules` | [`ListSchedulesRequest`](#listschedulesrequest) | [`ListSchedulesResponse`](#listschedulesresponse) | ListSchedules returns one namespace's schedules, ordered by name, narrowed by filters. A filter on id, name or orkflow_name is decided before a schedule is described, so a narrowed listing describes only what it may return. Every row it returns is described on the cluster for this call; a row the cluster could not describe is still listed, carrying unavailable_reason, on the terms ListPools narrows rather than refuses. |
| `GetSchedule` | [`GetScheduleRequest`](#getschedulerequest) | [`GetScheduleResponse`](#getscheduleresponse) | GetSchedule reads one schedule by name, with its next fire times and recent fires. A schedule of another namespace is NotFound. |
| `UpdateSchedule` | [`UpdateScheduleRequest`](#updateschedulerequest) | [`UpdateScheduleResponse`](#updatescheduleresponse) | UpdateSchedule REPLACES a schedule's mutable fields: version pin, input, description and spec. The orkflow a schedule is bound to is immutable, as a trigger's is: rebinding is delete then create. Last writer wins; see the request for why there is no etag. |
| `PauseSchedule` | [`PauseScheduleRequest`](#pauseschedulerequest) | [`PauseScheduleResponse`](#pausescheduleresponse) | PauseSchedule stops fires without deleting anything. The reason is kept by the cluster as the schedule's note and rendered on every read. |
| `ResumeSchedule` | [`ResumeScheduleRequest`](#resumeschedulerequest) | [`ResumeScheduleResponse`](#resumescheduleresponse) | ResumeSchedule lets a paused schedule fire again. |
| `FireSchedule` | [`FireScheduleRequest`](#fireschedulerequest) | [`FireScheduleResponse`](#firescheduleresponse) | FireSchedule fires once, now, as Temporal's TriggerImmediately does. It works on a paused schedule. The fire's run id is not known when this returns: it appears in recent_fires once the fire has prepared, and `run list --filter origin.kind=SCHEDULE --filter origin.id=<id>` lists it. |
| `BackfillSchedule` | [`BackfillScheduleRequest`](#backfillschedulerequest) | [`BackfillScheduleResponse`](#backfillscheduleresponse) | BackfillSchedule fires once for every nominal time the spec names in [start, end], as if that time passed now, under the overlap policy. Each backfilled run's origin.reference is its nominal time. |
| `DeleteSchedule` | [`DeleteScheduleRequest`](#deleteschedulerequest) | [`DeleteScheduleResponse`](#deletescheduleresponse) | DeleteSchedule removes the schedule. Runs it already started continue; a fire in progress finishes what it was doing. A repeat is NotFound. |

### StatsService

StatsService answers one question — "how is this namespace doing?" — from
the two records that already exist. It adds no write path, keeps no counter
and stores nothing: a number here is derived on read, or it is not reported.

The two sources are the cluster's own index of executions (live runs, and
how long the finished ones took) and the run archive's INDEX, whose keys
carry a run's namespace, orkflow, status and time. Neither is this process's
memory, so any replica answers identically — including one that started
nothing and holds no state of its own.

A counter would have been cheaper to read and impossible to trust: it is a
third record of a fact two records already hold, and the day it disagrees
with them there is no way to tell which is lying. Deriving on read cannot
drift, and the cost is bounded by a short-lived cache whose age every answer
carries (computed_at).

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/stats.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetStats` | [`GetStatsRequest`](#getstatsrequest) | [`GetStatsResponse`](#getstatsresponse) | GetStats reports one namespace's runs over one time window. |
| `GetFailureBreakdown` | [`GetFailureBreakdownRequest`](#getfailurebreakdownrequest) | [`GetFailureBreakdownResponse`](#getfailurebreakdownresponse) | GetFailureBreakdown groups one namespace's FAILED runs over one window by the dimensions the caller names. It is the read that makes the §4 failure categories pay: a category nobody counts is a comment.<br><br>It reads run BODIES — one per failed run in the window — which GetStats deliberately never does. The discriminating facts are not in the index key, and widening the key would be a migration and a second copy of the body. So the cost is bounded three ways instead: by the window, by the failed subset of it, and by a scan budget that FAILS the call rather than answering from a subset (see GetFailureBreakdownResponse). |
| `GetFlakeIndex` | [`GetFlakeIndexRequest`](#getflakeindexrequest) | [`GetFlakeIndexResponse`](#getflakeindexresponse) | GetFlakeIndex groups one namespace's dispatched tasks over one window by the dimensions the caller names and reports, per group, how often a task needed more than one attempt. It is the one cross-run read of the per-attempt records the Orker writes: a SUCCEEDED run that retried is invisible to every other number this service reports, by construction.<br><br>It reads run BODIES — one per finished run in the window, not only the failed ones — and one attempt listing per dispatched task. That is more than GetFailureBreakdown reads and far more than GetStats, which reads none, so the cost is bounded the same three ways: by the window, by an optional orkflow, and by a scan budget that FAILS the call rather than answering from a subset (see GetFlakeIndexResponse). |
| `GetUsage` | [`GetUsageRequest`](#getusagerequest) | [`GetUsageResponse`](#getusageresponse) | GetUsage reports how much of the fleet one namespace RESERVED over one window: task-seconds, and cpu-seconds and GiB-seconds as each attempt's reservation multiplied by how long its Orker held it. It is the read a budget is held against, and the one the admission gate itself makes for an enforced budget.<br><br>It reads the archive index (keys), every finished run's body in the window, and every attempt record of those runs, so its cost is bounded three ways: by the window, by a whole-answer cache whose age every answer carries (computed_at), and by a scan bound that FAILS the call rather than answering from a subset (see GetUsageResponse). |

### SystemService

SystemService reports what this deployment is made of.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/system_service.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetSystemInfo` | [`GetSystemInfoRequest`](#getsysteminforequest) | [`GetSystemInfoResponse`](#getsysteminforesponse) | GetSystemInfo describes THE REPLICA THAT ANSWERED. Every field is configuration- or build-derived — read from the process's own configuration, not observed from the cluster — except server_time. Replicas of one release answer identically by construction; mid-rollout, build_id is exactly the field that differs, which is the point of it.<br><br>It is the one admin read that does not leave the process, and it is the one question only the process can answer: everything else an operator asks — which namespaces exist, which pools have Orkers, what those Orkers run — comes from the store or the cluster, so any replica gives the same reply. This one describes the replica in front of you, on purpose, because that is what an operator behind a load balancer needs |
| `GetRetentionPolicy` | [`GetRetentionPolicyRequest`](#getretentionpolicyrequest) | [`GetRetentionPolicyResponse`](#getretentionpolicyresponse) | GetRetentionPolicy reads the deployment's maximum run retention: the ceiling on every namespace's run_retention, and what a namespace that sets none inherits. Read from the store, so any replica answers it.<br><br>It is deployment-wide on purpose. Per-namespace retention is a field of orkstack.v1.Namespace (NamespaceService); this is the bound on all of them. |
| `UpdateRetentionPolicy` | [`UpdateRetentionPolicyRequest`](#updateretentionpolicyrequest) | [`UpdateRetentionPolicyResponse`](#updateretentionpolicyresponse) | UpdateRetentionPolicy changes the maximum. A non-positive or malformed duration is INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything is written. Lowering it below a namespace's explicit run_retention is FAILED_PRECONDITION naming that namespace — lower the namespace first. Namespaces that set nothing follow the new maximum immediately: finished runs already older than it are retired on the next cleanup pass. |
| `ListTelemetrySinks` | [`ListTelemetrySinksRequest`](#listtelemetrysinksrequest) | [`ListTelemetrySinksResponse`](#listtelemetrysinksresponse) | ListTelemetrySinks names the telemetry sinks this deployment declared (ORK_TELEMETRY_SINKS), so a namespace admin can choose one by name. Names only: endpoints and headers are the operator's and never leave the process. CONFIGURATION-DERIVED; "default" is always present. |
| `GetImagePolicy` | [`GetImagePolicyRequest`](#getimagepolicyrequest) | [`GetImagePolicyResponse`](#getimagepolicyresponse) | GetImagePolicy reads the deployment's image supply-chain floor: whether a `uses:` may be a mutable tag, which registries images may come from, and which signing keys a namespace may require by name. Read from the store, so any replica answers it. A deployment that never wrote one answers the EMPTY policy with updated_at unset — that is a real answer (everything is permitted), not a missing document.<br><br>Deployment-wide on purpose. The per-namespace tightening is a field of orkstack.v1.Namespace (require_signed_by); this is the floor under all of them. |
| `UpdateImagePolicy` | [`UpdateImagePolicyRequest`](#updateimagepolicyrequest) | [`UpdateImagePolicyResponse`](#updateimagepolicyresponse) | UpdateImagePolicy replaces the floor. Every entry and key is validated before anything is written (INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the entry). An allowed_registries list that excludes an activity of this engine's catalog is FAILED_PRECONDITION naming the activities — widen the list or change ORK_ACTIVITY_CATALOG first, because a floor that silently refuses every `uses: shell` is not a floor an operator meant. Removing a signing key a namespace still names is FAILED_PRECONDITION naming the namespace — clear the namespace first. Definitions already stored are untouched; they are re-checked at their next submit. |
| `ListReleases` | [`ListReleasesRequest`](#listreleasesrequest) | [`ListReleasesResponse`](#listreleasesresponse) | ListReleases is the deployment's releases as the cluster routes them: which one takes new runs, which one is ramping and by how much, which ones are still finishing runs, and — for every release that does not take new runs — every reason it may not start to (Release.blockers). DERIVED on read from the cluster and from the Orker inventory (ActivityService.ListOrkers); nothing is stored, so any replica answers identically, including a replica of another release. A deployment no release of which has registered with the cluster answers versioned = false and no releases: an answer, not an error.<br><br>Filters select release rows only; every other response field is the deployment's, unfiltered, and blockers are still judged against the whole deployment. A build_id EQUALS filter counts only that release; an id the cluster does not know is an EMPTY list, never NOT_FOUND: `orkctl release wait` relies on it to tell "forgotten after draining" from an error. |
| `RampRelease` | [`RampReleaseRequest`](#rampreleaserequest) | [`RampReleaseResponse`](#rampreleaseresponse) | RampRelease sends `percent` of new runs to one release that is not current, and the rest to the current release. percent 0 stops the ramp of the release that is ramping. A ramp above 0 is FAILED_PRECONDITION, naming every blocker, whenever ListReleases reports one for that release, and nothing is written. Runs already executing are never moved. |
| `PromoteRelease` | [`PromoteReleaseRequest`](#promotereleaserequest) | [`PromoteReleaseResponse`](#promotereleaseresponse) | PromoteRelease makes one release take every new run. FAILED_PRECONDITION, naming every blocker, whenever ListReleases reports one for it, and nothing is written. Promoting the current release is a no-op success. Runs already executing on the previous release finish there and are never moved. `orkctl release rollback` is this RPC aimed at a release that was current before. |

### TriggerService

TriggerService manages inbound run starters. A trigger is bound to ONE
orkflow in one namespace, and an external caller presents that trigger's
bearer token over plain HTTP to start a run of it.

It is the mirror image of WebhookService, not a variant of it. A webhook is
OUTBOUND and deployment-wide unless it names a scope: OrkStack calls the
subscriber when a run it covers changes state. A trigger is INBOUND and orkflow-scoped: the caller calls
OrkStack, authenticating as the trigger. The orkflow coordinates come from
the stored record and never from the request, so whoever holds a token can
only start the orkflow the trigger was created for.

The secret is handed back exactly once, at creation, on the same terms as
RegisterWebhookResponse.secret: a listing never carries it again.

A trigger may carry a name, which is how an automation document addresses
it (docs/AUTOMATION.md); UpdateTrigger renames and re-pins in place.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/trigger_service.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateTrigger` | [`CreateTriggerRequest`](#createtriggerrequest) | [`CreateTriggerResponse`](#createtriggerresponse) |  |
| `ListTriggers` | [`ListTriggersRequest`](#listtriggersrequest) | [`ListTriggersResponse`](#listtriggersresponse) |  |
| `UpdateTrigger` | [`UpdateTriggerRequest`](#updatetriggerrequest) | [`UpdateTriggerResponse`](#updatetriggerresponse) | UpdateTrigger REPLACES a trigger's mutable fields — name, pinned version, description — in place. Its id, namespace, orkflow and bearer token never change: an update never re-issues a token, and the URL an external caller holds keeps working. Binding a trigger to another orkflow is delete then create. Last writer wins, and an update never brings back a trigger that was deleted meanwhile: that is NotFound. |
| `DeleteTrigger` | [`DeleteTriggerRequest`](#deletetriggerrequest) | [`DeleteTriggerResponse`](#deletetriggerresponse) |  |

### WebhookService

WebhookService manages run-event subscriptions. A subscription is
deployment-wide unless it names a scope: a namespace, an orkflow, a task,
each an exact match and each empty meaning "every". Delivery is
deliberately outside this management contract; callers never receive the
stored signing secret after registration.

What a delivery DID is a record, not a queue: one immutable object per
settled delivery (metadata/deliveries/…), written after the dispatcher
returned and read by nothing that decides what to send. ListDeliveries and
GetDelivery read it; RedeliverWebhook is one operator-initiated synchronous
POST, recorded as a new delivery. Nothing here retries on its own.

A subscription scoped to a namespace may carry a name; UpdateWebhook
changes it in place.

Defined in `proto/orkstack/v1/webhook_service.proto`.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RegisterWebhook` | [`RegisterWebhookRequest`](#registerwebhookrequest) | [`RegisterWebhookResponse`](#registerwebhookresponse) |  |
| `ListWebhooks` | [`ListWebhooksRequest`](#listwebhooksrequest) | [`ListWebhooksResponse`](#listwebhooksresponse) |  |
| `UpdateWebhook` | [`UpdateWebhookRequest`](#updatewebhookrequest) | [`UpdateWebhookResponse`](#updatewebhookresponse) | UpdateWebhook REPLACES a subscription's mutable fields — name, url, events and scope — in place. Its id and signing secret never change, so a receiver keeps verifying and a delivery record's webhook_id keeps naming the same subscription. Last writer wins; an update never brings back a subscription deleted meanwhile (NotFound). The secret is never in the request or the response. |
| `DeleteWebhook` | [`DeleteWebhookRequest`](#deletewebhookrequest) | [`DeleteWebhookResponse`](#deletewebhookresponse) |  |
| `ListDeliveries` | [`ListDeliveriesRequest`](#listdeliveriesrequest) | [`ListDeliveriesResponse`](#listdeliveriesresponse) | ListDeliveries lists delivery records newest first, bounded and paginated. A scan that would examine more keys than the engine's budget allows before filling a page is REFUSED (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) naming the budget, never answered from the subset it managed to read. |
| `GetDelivery` | [`GetDeliveryRequest`](#getdeliveryrequest) | [`GetDeliveryResponse`](#getdeliveryresponse) | GetDelivery returns one record by id. |
| `RedeliverWebhook` | [`RedeliverWebhookRequest`](#redeliverwebhookrequest) | [`RedeliverWebhookResponse`](#redeliverwebhookresponse) | RedeliverWebhook POSTs one delivery again — once, now, synchronously, signed with the subscription's current secret, embedding the run as it reads today — and returns the NEW record. The operator is the retry policy: this RPC never queues, never retries, and never runs unattended. |

## Messages

### ActivityInfo

ActivityInfo is one catalog entry, resolved.

resolved_at is a READ-MODEL field on a live catalog read, and is unrelated
to the ImageRef.resolved_at that activity.proto reserves: nothing hashes it,
and it is never stored in a version document.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | catalog key, e.g. "shell"; empty for InspectActivity of a raw reference |
| `reference` | `string` | as configured, e.g. ghcr.io/orkstack/activity-shell:0.1 |
| `index_digest` | `string` | resolved, "sha256:&lt;64 hex>" |
| `media_type` | `string` |  |
| `platforms` | repeated `string` |  |
| `resolved_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `interface` | [`ActivityInterface`](#activityinterface) | interface is what the image declares about its `with:` block, read from the org.orkstack.activity.interface label of the resolved image's config (§4.3 step 7). Unset when the image carries no label, when the label could not be read (interface_error says why), or when the reference did not resolve (index_digest is then empty too).<br><br>It is a READ-MODEL field exactly as resolved_at is: derived from immutable, digest-addressed content on every read, hashed by nothing, stored nowhere. |
| `interface_error` | `string` | interface_error is non-empty when the image carries the label but it could not be turned into an ActivityInterface — malformed JSON, a schema_version this engine does not read, a vocabulary word outside the contract — or when the index advertised no platform manifest to read a config from. It distinguishes "declares nothing" from "declares something this engine cannot read". Empty whenever interface is set. |

### ActivityInterface

ActivityInterface is what an image declares about its `with:` block. The
label org.orkstack.activity.interface holds this message's protojson
encoding (lowerCamel names), verbatim.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `int32` | schema_version is 1. Any other value is a manifest this engine does not read and is reported through ActivityInfo.interface_error. |
| `fields` | map&lt;`string`, [`FieldSchema`](#fieldschema)&gt; | fields are the top-level `with:` keys every op reads (or, for an image with no op selector, the whole `with:` block). The key is the `with:` key, byte for byte. |
| `ops` | map&lt;`string`, [`OpSchema`](#opschema)&gt; | ops, when non-empty, says the image selects its operation with the `op` key of docs/ACTIVITY_IMAGES.md: the map key is the op's name and the value is the keys that op reads in addition to `fields`. `op` itself is then implicitly declared {type: "string"} and must not appear in `fields`. A key may not be declared both in `fields` and under an op. |
| `default_op` | `string` | default_op is the op the image runs when `op` is absent, and must be a key of ops. Empty with non-empty ops means `op` is required. |
| `values` | map&lt;`string`, [`FieldSchema`](#fieldschema)&gt; | values is documentary: the keys the image writes to values.json. Nothing checks it; `orkctl activity inspect` and the Activities page render it so an author knows what `.tasks.<id>.output.<key>` may reference. |

### ApplyOrkflowRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `yaml` | `string` | raw DSL document |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace selects where the document is applied. Empty honours the document's own `namespace:` (itself empty = "default"); a non-empty value must EQUAL the document's namespace, or the document names none and is applied INTO this one. The two are never allowed to disagree silently: a file that says `namespace: payments` applied with -n staging is a mistake one of the two made, and guessing which would store the definition somewhere its author cannot find it. |
| `base_version` | `string` | base_version is the stored version this edit was derived from — its PROVENANCE and the anchor a diff is taken against, not the concurrency token. ANY stored version is a valid base: editing an old one is how a user forks forward from it, and the apply lands as the new head with the `current` pointer untouched. A non-empty value that names no stored version is NotFound, naming it.<br><br>It is a VERSION token rather than a content hash. Both name where an edit came from; only the token names something the user can act on — `orkctl orkflow diff <name> <base_version> <head>` shows exactly what arrived underneath the edit. A hash names nothing. |
| `expected_head_version` | `string` | expected_head_version is the optimistic-concurrency token: the head version the editor observed when it fetched. Non-empty and different from the stored head is refused (FailedPrecondition) naming both, WHATEVER base was chosen — so an edit made while somebody else applied is reported instead of landing beside a newer version nobody looked at.<br><br>Empty with an empty base_version is unchecked, which is what a plain `orkctl apply file.yaml` sends. Empty with a non-empty base_version is InvalidArgument naming both fields: a base is provenance, not a head claim, and an editor that read a base also read the head it was under.<br><br>Two fields because there are two facts. With one, the server cannot tell "derived from an old version on purpose" from "derived from a head that has since moved", and the first is the whole point of this contract. |

### AuditRecord

AuditRecord is one control-plane WRITE, recorded immutably at the moment
the handler returned — succeeded or refused.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `int32` | schema_version is 1. A reader refuses a record whose version it does not know rather than guessing at its fields. |
| `id` | `string` | id is opaque, shaped "aud-{stamp}-{16 hex}", where stamp is the store's sortable UTC layout and the hex is 8 bytes from crypto/rand. It is the key's leaf. Nothing derives meaning from it: the record's own `at` is the time, and the key's day segments are the store's, not a client's. |
| `at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | at is the engine's clock when the handler returned. |
| `principal` | `string` | principal is what the deployment's gateway asserted in the Ork-Principal request header, recorded verbatim (bounded, control characters replaced) and NEVER trusted as authentication: OrkStack has no identity system and this field does not invent one. Empty when no header was present, which every client renders as "unattributed" rather than as a name, because a blank that looks like a user is worse than an honest gap. |
| `source_address` | `string` | source_address is the TCP peer the engine accepted the request from, as connect.Request.Peer().Addr reports it. Behind a gateway it is the gateway's address; no forwarded-for header is consulted. |
| `action` | `string` | action is the user-facing name of the write: "namespace.update", "orkflow.apply", "trigger.create", "retention.update", … The complete set is the engine's audited-procedure table (internal/api/audit.go); a client filters by prefix (action^namespace.) and never needs to know the set. |
| `procedure` | `string` | procedure is the exact RPC, e.g. "/orkstack.v1.NamespaceService/UpdateNamespace", or the HTTP route for the legacy webhook adapter ("POST /v1/webhooks"). It is the machine-readable twin of action. |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace is the OrkStack namespace the write addressed, resolved ("default" spelled out), and EMPTY only for a deployment-wide target (retention policy, webhooks). Empty here never means "default". |
| `target` | `string` | target is the object the action addressed: an orkflow "name@version", a namespace name, a run id, a webhook or trigger id, or "deployment". |
| `detail` | `string` | detail is a short human-readable summary of what was asked — never a secret, never a token, never a request body. Bounded. |
| `succeeded` | `bool` | succeeded is whether the handler returned success. A refused write is a record too: who tried is evidence. |
| `error_code` | `string` | error_code is the Connect code name ("failed_precondition", "not_found", …) when succeeded is false; empty otherwise. |

### AwaitSpec

AwaitSpec makes a Task an awaited task: it starts no container and reaches
no Orker, and the run waits until the task is resolved from outside the run
— completed with values, or rejected with a reason — or its deadline passes.
Part of canonicalOrkflow(Task), emitted ONLY when set (see Task.pin).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `timeout_seconds` | `int32` | timeout_seconds is the deadline, from the moment the task starts awaiting. Required: 1 to 2592000 (30 days). |
| `callback` | `bool` | callback asks SubmitRun to mint a one-time bearer token for this await and disclose it once, in SubmitRunResponse.await_callbacks, so a caller outside the deployment's API can resolve it over plain HTTP. False means the await is resolved through RunService.ResolveAwait only. |
| `schema` | `google.protobuf.Struct` | schema declares the values a completion must carry, in the vocabulary Orkflow.inputs uses — a map from key to {type, required}; no default. Unset means any JSON object is accepted. |

### Budget

Budget bounds how much of the fleet one namespace may RESERVE over a
rolling period. Its units are reservation × held time: the cpu and memory
an Orker granted each attempt (TaskAttempt.resources), multiplied by how
long that Orker held the attempt. They are not utilization, and every
surface that renders them says so: OrkStack reserves, the kernel measures,
and presenting the first as the second would be a number no measurement
produced.

Usage is derived on read (StatsService.GetUsage) from the runs this
namespace created inside the period that have FINISHED; a run still in
flight is counted when it finishes. Nothing counts usage as it happens, so
nothing can disagree with the records tomorrow.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu_seconds` | `int64` | cpu_seconds bounds reserved cpu × held time, in cpu-seconds. 0 means this dimension is not bounded. At least one of cpu_seconds and gib_seconds is above 0; a budget that bounds nothing is refused — clear it instead. |
| `gib_seconds` | `int64` | gib_seconds bounds reserved memory × held time, in GiB-seconds (memory bytes ÷ 2^30 × seconds). 0 means this dimension is not bounded. |
| `period` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | period is the rolling window a budget is held against, ending at the moment of the question. Required; at least 1h and at most 744h (31 days). A longer question is a report — `orkctl stats usage --since` — not a budget evaluated at every submit. |
| `enforce` | `bool` | enforce turns the budget from an observation into an admission rule. False — the default — reports usage against the budget on every read and never refuses anything, and costs nothing at submit. True refuses every new run of the namespace with FAILED_PRECONDITION while measured usage over the trailing period is at or above any bounded dimension. Either way an accepted run is never touched (AGENTS.md §15). |

| `miss_reason` | `string` | miss_reason is set for MISS only: a stable token from the table in docs/DSL.md "Caching" — MEMO_ABSENT, MEMO_EXPIRED, SOURCE_COMMIT_GONE, … — a string, not an enum, so a reader of an older build still prints a reason it has never heard of. It is never a failure code: it never appears in TaskRun.error. |
| `miss_detail` | `string` | miss_detail is the Orker's sentence for the miss, at most 1 KiB. |
| `source` | [`CacheSource`](#cachesource) | source is set for HIT only. |
| `memo_written` | `bool` | memo_written / memo_write_error report the best-effort memo write that follows a fresh commit (MISS or BYPASSED). Both are decided AFTER commit.json is written, so neither is ever set on ActivityCommit.cache, and an adopted result carries neither. |
| `memo_write_error` | `string` |  |
| `key_components` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; | key_components are the named digests the key was computed from — what lets an operator see WHICH input changed between a miss and the run that wrote the old memo. Set ONLY on TaskAttempt.cache and in CacheMemo; never on ExecuteTaskResult, TaskRun or ActivityCommit, so run history stays small. |

### CacheSource

CacheSource names the commit a memo points at — the one a hit reused.

### CacheSpec

CacheSpec opts ONE task into memoization across runs (docs/DSL.md
"Caching"). Declaring it is the author's assertion that the task is a pure
function of what it is given — its image, command, env, secrets' names and
sources, network mode, rendered config.json, run.json, staged input files
and, for a fan-out item, its item — which OrkStack cannot verify. Part of
canonicalOrkflow(Task) only when set (see Task.pin); never part of a memo
key.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ttl_seconds` | `int32` | ttl_seconds bounds how old a memoized result this task may reuse, measured from when the result was committed. 0 means no bound of the task's own; the deployment's ORK_CACHE_MAX_TTL caps it either way. |
| `scope` | [`CacheScope`](#cachescope) | scope: ORKFLOW (what the compiler writes when absent) or NAMESPACE. |

### CacheUsageRow

CacheUsageRow is one cached task's outcomes over the window's finished
runs: every TaskRun (and fan-out item) whose cache.outcome is set.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `hits` | `int64` |  |
| `misses` | `int64` |  |
| `bypassed` | `int64` |  |

| `hit_rate_defined` | `bool` |  |
| `reused` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | reused is the sum, over hits, of the source attempt's duration (source.finished_at - source.started_at): the producing attempts' time these hits did not spend again. Stated as that, never as "saved". |

### Delivery

Delivery is one settled webhook delivery: what OrkStack sent, what the
receiver answered, and nothing about what the receiver did with it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `int32` | schema_version is 1. A reader skips a record whose version it does not know rather than guessing at its fields. |
| `id` | `string` | id is the value the receiver saw in X-Ork-Delivery, shaped "dlv-{stamp}-{16 hex}" where stamp is the store's sortable UTC layout at the instant the delivery was queued (created_at) and the hex is 8 bytes from crypto/rand. The stamp is the store's coordinate for the record's key; no client parses it — created_at is the time. |
| `webhook_id` | `string` |  |
| `event` | [`EventType`](#eventtype) |  |
| `run_id` | `string` |  |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace is the run's resolved namespace ("default" spelled out). |
| `orkflow_name` | `string` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` | task_id and attempt are set for a task outcome delivery (docs/UI_CLI_PARITY.md "Scoped subscriptions and task outcome events") and empty/zero for a run transition. |
| `attempt` | `int32` |  |
| `status` | [`Status`](#status) | status is the transition's status as the body's "status" carried it. |
| `url` | `string` | url is the subscription's URL as it was POSTed to. |
| `delivered` | `bool` |  |
| `signature` | `string` | signature is the X-Ork-Signature value sent ("sha256=…"), or empty when the delivery was unsigned. It is what the record proves was sent; the secret itself is never here. |
| `body_sha256` | `string` | body_sha256 is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes POSTed, and body_bytes their length. The body is not stored: the run is readable at GetRun, and a second copy would be a second version of the truth. |
| `body_bytes` | `int64` |  |
| `attempts` | repeated [`DeliveryAttempt`](#deliveryattempt) |  |
| `event_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | event_at is the transition's own timestamp (X-Ork-Timestamp, the body's "timestamp"); created_at is when the notifier queued the delivery; settled_at is when the dispatcher returned. |
| `created_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `settled_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `redelivery_of` | `string` | redelivery_of names the delivery this one repeats, when an operator asked for it through RedeliverWebhook. Empty for a delivery the engine made on its own. |

### DeliveryAttempt

DeliveryAttempt is one POST of one delivery, as pkg/webhooks.Attempt
recorded it.

| `duration` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | how long the request itself took |
| `at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | when the request was started |

### DescribeOrkerResult

DescribeOrkerResult is the pool-liveness probe's payload: a pool proves it
is alive by answering DescribeOrker (§6.5).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orker_id` | `string` |  |
| `build_id` | `string` |  |
| `pool` | `string` |  |
| `runtime_name` | `string` | "docker" |
| `runtime_version` | `string` |  |
| `security_profile` | `string` | the profile id the Orker enforces (§9.2) |
| `max_concurrent` | `int32` | max_concurrent is ORK_ORKER_MAX_CONCURRENT: how many tasks this Orker runs at once, the size of its task worker's activity slots. |
| `rootless` | `bool` |  |
| `max_concurrent_pins` | `int32` | max_concurrent_pins is ORK_ORKER_MAX_PINS: how many pins this Orker hosts at once. 0 means it hosts none, and a submit that pins a task to this Orker's pool is refused at submit rather than left waiting. |
| `cordoned` | `bool` | cordoned is this Orker's process-local cordon flag. It is NEVER stored anywhere but the process: a restarted Orker answers false. |
| `cordon_reason` | `string` | cordon_reason is the reason given to CordonOrker; empty when not cordoned. |
| `cordoned_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | cordoned_at is when the flag was last set; unset when not cordoned. |
| `running_tasks` | `int32` | running_tasks is how many ExecuteTask activities this Orker has in flight right now, pinned members included. Counted in the process; it is a measurement, not a projection. |
| `open_pins` | `int32` | open_pins is how many pins this Orker currently hosts: pins it accepted and has not closed. Counted from the pin openings in flight, so it is exact from the instant a pin is accepted, before its first member arrives. It never exceeds max_concurrent_pins. |
| `pins` | repeated [`OpenPin`](#openpin) | pins details each open pin, ordered by run_id. len(pins) == open_pins. |
| `each_supported` | `bool` | each_supported is true on an Orker that implements fan-out items: it honours ExecuteTaskInput.each (task.json `each`, .each in with:) and stages EachUpstream. An Orker built before it answers false (unset), and submit refuses an Orkflow with a fan-out on such a pool rather than let it run items without their item or a dependent without its items. |
| `cache_supported` | `bool` | cache_supported is true on an Orker that implements the memo step. An Orker built before it answers false (unset), and submit refuses an Orkflow with a cached task on its pool: the SDK's default payload converter refuses unknown fields, so such an Orker would FAIL every cached task's attempt on decoding ExecuteTaskInput.cache. |
| `join_supported` | `bool` | join_supported is true on an Orker that reads ExecuteTaskInput.join (task.json `join`). An Orker built before it answers false (unset), and submit refuses an Orkflow with a container failure handler on its pool: the SDK's default payload converter refuses unknown fields, so such an Orker would FAIL every attempt of a failure handler on decoding ExecuteTaskInput.join — the compensation step of a run that is already failing. |
| `capacity` | [`ResourceQuantity`](#resourcequantity) | capacity is what this Orker admits tasks within (orker.capacity.cpu and orker.capacity.memory). Unset when it declares none: it then admits by max_concurrent alone, as every Orker did before capacity existed. A dimension at 0 is not bounded. |
| `reserved` | [`ResourceQuantity`](#resourcequantity) | reserved is what stands reserved against capacity now: the per-task cap of every outstanding poll for a task, the request of every task it holds, pinned members included, and every container it has not yet removed. Unset when capacity is. A pinned member is counted but never made to wait, so reserved can exceed capacity by what open pins run. |
| `max_request` | [`ResourceQuantity`](#resourcequantity) | max_request is the per-task cap (orker.resources.max_cpu and max_memory): the largest request this Orker runs. Submit refuses a task whose request no answering Orker of its pool could hold (RESOURCES_UNSATISFIABLE). Unset on an Orker built before it existed. |
| `default_request` | [`ResourceQuantity`](#resourcequantity) | default_request is what a task that requests nothing is given (orker.resources.default_cpu and default_memory). |

### DiffRunsRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `from_run_id` | `string` |  |
| `to_run_id` | `string` |  |
| `namespace` | `string` | empty = the default namespace; BOTH runs resolve in it |
| `only` | repeated `string` | only restricts the comparison to the named fields, in the vocabulary RunFieldDiff.field uses plus the two run-level names "definition" and "input". Empty means every field. An unknown name is InvalidArgument naming the valid ones. Narrowing also narrows the READS: a request that names neither "image" nor "platform_digest" never opens the attempt store or the orkflow store.<br><br>"presence" is ALWAYS compared, whatever only names: a task that exists in one run and not the other always yields its presence row, so narrowing can never make an added or removed task count as identical. Naming "presence" is accepted and redundant. It costs no read beyond the two runs themselves. |

### DiffRunsResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | [`Run`](#run) | from / to are the two runs, SHALLOW: task_runs, input and output are cleared, because the differences below and input_unified_diff already carry what a client needs of them, and a run's input may be large. Every other Run field (id, orkflow, version, status, error, times, namespace, definition digest, telemetry, and any field a later contract adds) is carried as GetRun would carry it. |
| `to` | [`Run`](#run) |  |
| `same_orkflow` | `bool` | orkflow_name equal (namespace is equal by construction) |
| `same_definition_digest` | `bool` | orkflow_definition_digest equal |
| `input_unified_diff` | `string` | input_unified_diff is dsl.Unified over the canonical, indented JSON of the two inputs (keys sorted, integers without fraction), labelled "&lt;run id>/input.json" on each side. Empty when the inputs are identical under that canonical form, or when "input" was excluded by `only`. |
| `differences` | repeated [`RunFieldDiff`](#runfielddiff) | differences is ordered: run-level rows first, then the from-run's tasks in its task_runs order, then tasks present only in the to-run in that run's order; within a task, fields in the order the field comment on RunFieldDiff lists them. The order is the contract; clients render it as given. |
| `tasks_compared` | `int32` | tasks_compared is the number of distinct task ids across both runs. |
| `tasks_identical` | `int32` | tasks_identical is the number of tasks with NO row: every compared field equal and available on both sides. A task whose evidence is missing on either side is not identical, whatever its other fields say; nor is a task present in only one run, which always has its presence row. |
| `evidence_unavailable` | `int32` | evidence_unavailable counts rows with at least one unavailable side. |
| `fields_compared` | repeated `string` | fields_compared is the resolved field list — every field when `only` is empty, else `only` plus "presence" — in canonical order, so a client can say what was and was not compared. It is exhaustive: every RunFieldDiff.field in differences is one of its entries. |

### EachSource

EachSource is where a fan-out task's array lives: compiled at apply from
EachSpec.over and stamped into the immutable version document, as
Task.image is for `uses:`. Workflow code and the Orker read it and never
parse `over`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | `string` | input names a declared input (.inputs.&lt;input>); task_id names a task in the fan-out's needs closure (.tasks.&lt;task_id>.output). Exactly one is set. |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `path` | repeated `string` | path is the object keys below that root, outermost first. It is empty only for an input declared `type: array`; a task source always has at least one key, because a values.json is an object. There is no array index and no wildcard. |

### EachSpec

EachSpec makes a Task a fan-out: ONE node of the DAG that runs as one item
per element of an array read at run time — every item the same image, with
the same needs, pool, resources, timeout and retry policy (docs/DSL.md
"Fan-out"). Part of canonicalOrkflow(Task), emitted ONLY when set (see
Task.pin).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `over` | `string` | over is the reference exactly as the author wrote it: one template action naming an input or an upstream task's output, never an expression. |
| `as` | `string` | as is the name .each.&lt;as> binds an item to. The compiler writes "item" when the document names none, so a stored value is never empty. |
| `max_items` | `int32` | max_items is the author's bound, 1..10000; the sum over every fan-out of one Orkflow is at most 10000, and at most the deployment's ORK_EACH_MAX_ITEMS (1000 unless the deployment raises it). An array longer than this fails the task EACH_TOO_MANY_ITEMS before any item runs. |
| `max_parallel` | `int32` | max_parallel bounds how many items are in flight at once; 0 means no bound of the task's own. |
| `source` | [`EachSource`](#eachsource) | source is over, compiled at apply (EachSource). |

Such an event is EVENT_TYPE_TASK_LOG carrying the item's terminal status — the precedent markSkipped and markCanceled set, since the Event contract has no item type — and TaskRun.items is the authoritative record. Unset on every other event. |

bundle, and a client must discard what it received.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `bytes` |  |
| `last` | `bool` |  |

| Field | Type | Description |

| `run_id` | `string` |  |

| `exclude_logs` | `bool` | exclude_logs and exclude_artifacts drop the attempts' stdout.log and stderr.log, and the tasks' output artifacts, from the bundle. They are spelled as exclusions so that the proto3 zero value — an empty request — is the COMPLETE bundle: a caller that asks for nothing in particular gets everything. values.json, commit.json and attempt records are never excluded; they are what makes the bundle evidence. |

The small members (the archive body, the definition, commits, attempt records) are still read and hashed; artifact and log objects are stat'ed, never read. |

### FailureGroup

FailureGroup is every failed run in the window that shares one fingerprint.

A dimension NOT in the request's group_by is empty here and means "not
grouped by". A dimension that IS in group_by and is empty means one of two
things, told apart by attempt_evidence_missing: for IMAGE and PHASE with a
nonzero attempt_evidence_missing it means "unavailable — the attempt record
was reclaimed or never written"; otherwise it means the snapshot genuinely
carries no value (a run-level failure has no task, a task that never
reached an Orker has no pool or orker, a snapshot written before a field
existed). Clients render the first as `unavailable` and the second as `-`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `code` | `string` |  |
| `category` | [`FailureCategory`](#failurecategory) |  |
| `image_pinned` | `string` |  |
| `pool` | `string` |  |
| `phase` | `string` |  |
| `orker_id` | `string` |  |
| `run_count` | `int64` |  |
| `first_seen` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | first_seen and last_seen are the creation times of the group's oldest and newest runs — the same coordinate the window is measured in. |
| `last_seen` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `example_run_ids` | repeated `string` | example_run_ids holds at most 3 of the group's runs, newest created first. Ids are never compared with each other (AGENTS.md §7). |
| `attempt_evidence_missing` | `int64` | attempt_evidence_missing counts this group's runs whose attempt record could not be read, so image and phase were unavailable for them. It is only ever nonzero when the response's attempt_evidence_read is true. |

### FieldFilter

FieldFilter is one predicate over one field of the listed object.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `field` | `string` | field is a path the request's (filterable) option declares: proto field names of the listed message, dotted through a nested message ("origin.kind"), or "labels.&lt;key>" for one key of a labels map, the key verbatim after the first "labels." (it may contain dots). |
| `op` | [`FilterOperator`](#filteroperator) |  |
| `values` | repeated `string` | values in the spelling `orkctl --json` prints: text verbatim, an enum value's short name ("FAILED"), true/false, an RFC 3339 instant with a zone. docs/UI_CLI_PARITY.md "Filtering lists" states the matching rules. |

### FieldSchema

FieldSchema is one `with:` key's declaration. It is EXACTLY the
vocabulary an Orkflow's `inputs:` already has (docs/DSL.md, "Inputs")
and not one word more: no pattern, no range, no enum, no nesting.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `string` | type is one of "string", "number", "boolean", "object", "array", or several joined by "\|" (string\|object\|array) for a key that accepts any of them. |
| `required` | `bool` | required means the image refuses to run without this key. A field with a default is never required (the two contradict; the manifest is rejected). |
| `default` | `google.protobuf.Value` | default is documentary: what the image assumes when the key is absent. The engine never writes it into `with:`. When set, its JSON type must be one of `type`'s; null is not a default (omit the field). |

### FlakeGroup

FlakeGroup is every (run, task) pair in the window whose attempts share
one group key, counted by run.

A dimension NOT in the request's group_by is empty here and means "not
grouped by". A dimension that IS in group_by and is empty means the record
genuinely carries no value (a record written before the field existed);
there is no "unavailable" case for a keyed dimension, because a task whose
records are gone is not in any record-keyed group at all — it is counted
in runs_evidence_missing instead.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `pool` | `string` |  |
| `orker_id` | `string` |  |
| `phase` | `string` |  |
| `image_pinned` | `string` |  |
| `runs_observed` | `int64` | runs_observed is how many distinct runs contributed a task with at least one attempt carrying this group's key. It is the denominator. |
| `runs_retried` | `int64` | runs_retried is how many of those runs had a NON-FINAL attempt carrying this key — an attempt below the task's highest, which by construction did not complete the task and caused the next one to be scheduled. It is the numerator. Keyed by ORKER, this attributes a retry to the Orker whose attempt failed, never to the one that then succeeded. |
| `retry_rate` | `double` | retry_rate is runs_retried / runs_observed, between 0 and 1. |
| `retry_rate_defined` | `bool` | retry_rate_defined is false when runs_observed is 0. That happens only for a body-keyed group: a task the window dispatched in some run but for which no run in the window has a record. Render "unavailable", never 0%. |
| `runs_evidence_missing` | `int64` | runs_evidence_missing is how many distinct runs dispatched a task with this group's body key and hold NO attempt record for it: the records were reclaimed on the run's retention schedule, or the Orker's best-effort write never landed. Those runs are in neither runs_observed nor runs_retried. Exact when the response's body_keyed is true; 0 otherwise, because a task with no record has no orker, phase or image to be keyed by, and only the response total is then meaningful. |
| `p50_attempts` | `int32` | p50_attempts and p95_attempts are the median and 95th percentile, by nearest rank over runs_observed samples, of how many attempts carrying this key one run took (the maximum over that run's member tasks). For a body-keyed group that is simply the task's attempt count; for an ORKER-keyed group it is how many attempts ran on that Orker in that run. Nearest rank: every value here is a count some run actually reached. |
| `p95_attempts` | `int32` |  |
| `retry_attempts` | `int64` | retry_attempts is the number of non-final RECORDED attempts carrying this key, summed over the group's runs — the attempts the retries are attributed to, and the population dominant_* is the mode of. |
| `unreported_attempts` | `int64` | unreported_attempts counts attempts numbered below a task's highest that have no record of their own: the Orker running them died or lost its heartbeat before it could file one. They are retries with no recorded cause. Exact when body_keyed; 0 otherwise, for the reason given on runs_evidence_missing. |
| `dominant_code` | `string` | dominant_code, dominant_category and dominant_phase are ONE triple — the (error.code, error.category, phase) that the most of retry_attempts share — never three independent modes, which could name a combination no attempt had. dominant_count is how many of retry_attempts share it. All four are unset when retry_attempts is 0. |
| `dominant_category` | [`FailureCategory`](#failurecategory) |  |
| `dominant_phase` | `string` |  |
| `dominant_count` | `int64` |  |
| `last_retried_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | last_retried_at is the creation time of the newest run in runs_retried — the coordinate the window is measured in. Unset when runs_retried is 0. |
| `example_run_ids` | repeated `string` | example_run_ids holds at most 3 of the group's retried runs, newest created first, so a row leads to a run page whose attempt timeline shows the retries. Ids are never compared with each other (AGENTS.md §7). |

### GetRunRequest

A run id addresses a run INSIDE a namespace, exactly as an orkflow name
does. It is unguessable, but unguessable is not a tenancy boundary: an id
travels into logs, tickets and CI transcripts, and CancelRun is a write. So
every request that carries one carries the namespace it is addressed in, on
the same rule as every other namespace field — empty is the default
namespace, never "any of them". A run of another namespace is NotFound, not
PermissionDenied: telling the two apart would confirm to a caller who may
not name the namespace that the id exists.
