### GetStatsRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | `string` | empty = the default namespace |
| `since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | since is the inclusive start of the window. Empty means lookback before the window ends, and lookback's own default is 24 hours. |
| `until` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | until is the exclusive end of the window. Empty means the moment the answer is computed. A window whose end is not after its start is refused rather than answered with zeros, which is a number that reads like a fact. |
| `lookback` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | lookback says how far back from `until` the window reaches, for the client that means "the last six hours" rather than a pair of instants. It is ignored when `since` is set.<br><br>It exists so that ONE clock decides a relative window. A client that resolved "six hours ago" itself would be pairing its own clock with the server's — the two ends of one window measured by two machines — and a client running a few minutes fast would silently ask about a window of the wrong length, or about one that ends before it starts. The times a window is compared against are the server's either way, so the arithmetic belongs there. |

### GetStatsResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `runs_by_status` | map&lt;`string`, `int64`&gt; | ONE WINDOW, ONE POPULATION. Every number below is about the same set of runs: the runs this namespace CREATED between window_since (inclusive) and window_until (exclusive). A run is counted in the window it was submitted in, whenever it happens to end, because that is the only instant both sources agree on — the archive index stamps a run by its creation time (internal/engine/archive.go, RunIndexTime) and the cluster's execution index carries its start.<br><br>The alternative — counting a run in the window it FINISHED in — was what the percentiles used to do, and one answer carrying both is a lie no field could correct: `orkctl stats --since 15m` over hour-long runs reported `succeeded 0 / failed 0 / rate unavailable` beside `p50 58m over 12 finished runs`, two populations printed as one.<br><br>The one exception is `running`, and it is stated where it is declared: it is a fact about NOW rather than about the window.<br><br>runs_by_status counts the window's runs. Keys are the lowercase, unprefixed status names: "running", "succeeded", "failed", "canceled". All four are always present, so a client renders a real zero rather than a blank.<br><br>There is deliberately no "pending" key. A run that has been accepted but has not started its first task is still one executing entry in the cluster's index, and telling the two apart means reading that run's history — one read per run, which is the cost this whole service is built to avoid. "running" therefore means "accepted and not finished", and the `running` list below is exactly the same set. A key that could only ever be answered by guessing is not reported at all. |
| `success_rate` | `double` | success_rate is succeeded / finished, between 0 and 1, over the window's runs that have finished. Canceled runs count as finished: a client that cancels half its runs has not succeeded at them, and hiding them would make the rate rise when things go wrong. |
| `success_rate_defined` | `bool` | success_rate_defined is false when the window finished no runs at all. A rate over nothing is not 0 — it is unanswerable, and 0 is the most alarming number a dashboard can show. Render "no data", never zero. |
| `p50_duration` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | p50_duration and p95_duration are the median and 95th percentile of how long the window's finished runs took, by nearest rank over the samples duration_sample_count reports.<br><br>"The window's finished runs" is the SAME set success_rate is a rate over: runs created inside the window that have since ended. A run created before the window and closed inside it is neither counted nor sampled, and one created inside it and still going is counted as running and sampled by neither. |
| `p95_duration` | `google.protobuf.Duration` |  |
| `duration_coverage_since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | duration_coverage_since is the instant the percentiles actually cover, which can be later than the window's start. How long a run took is known only while the cluster still holds its execution record; the archive index carries a run's status and time but not its duration, and reading bodies to recover one is the cost this service refuses.<br><br>So a 30-day window over a 3-day record answers for 3 days AND SAYS SO here, instead of quietly presenting three days of latency as thirty. It is also the one place the two sources can legitimately disagree about the one population: a run created before this instant is still counted from the archive, which keeps every run for ever, and can no longer be sampled from the cluster, which does not. |
| `duration_sample_count` | `int64` | duration_sample_count is how many runs the percentiles were computed from: the window's runs that have finished and whose execution record the cluster still holds. Zero means they are unavailable and the two durations above are unset — a client shows "unavailable", never "0s", which reads as instant success. |
| `most_failing` | repeated [`OrkflowFailures`](#orkflowfailures) | most_failing lists the orkflows with the most failed runs in the window, worst first, and only those that failed at least once. |
| `running` | repeated [`Run`](#run) | running is every run executing when the answer was computed, newest first. Each is the shallow projection an index can give — id, namespace, orkflow, status and start time. A run's tasks, input and output live elsewhere; GetRun reads them. |
| `pools` | repeated [`Pool`](#pool) | pools is the same pool health ListPools reports: every pool this namespace may dispatch onto, with the Orkers serving it right now. |
| `computed_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | computed_at is when these numbers were measured, which is not necessarily when they were asked for: an answer may be served from a short-lived cache. It is the age of every number here, on the wire, so a client can show it. |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace, window_since and window_until are the question that was actually answered, with an empty request resolved. A client that asked for "the default namespace, the last day" cannot label its own numbers without them, and it should not have to know the default's name to do it. |
| `window_since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `window_until` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |

ORKFLOW, TASK and POOL are accepted; TASK implies ORKFLOW, which is prepended when absent, because a task id names a task only within its orkflow. Every other value, a duplicate, or UNSPECIFIED is InvalidArgument: usage is not a failure, and code, category, image, phase and orker are not what a reservation is attributed to. |

### GetUsageResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `total` | [`UsageRow`](#usagerow) | total is the whole namespace over the window; every row sums into it. |
| `rows` | repeated [`UsageRow`](#usagerow) | rows is one per group, ordered by cpu_seconds desc, gib_seconds desc, task_seconds desc, then each keyed dimension ascending in group_by's enum order — total and clock-free, so two replicas produce the same table from the same bytes. Empty when group_by is. |
| `group_by` | repeated [`FailureGroupBy`](#failuregroupby) | group_by is the dimensions actually grouped by, TASK's implied ORKFLOW made explicit at the front. A client cannot label its columns without it. |
| `runs_in_window` | `int64` | THE POPULATION AND ITS EVIDENCE — the same definitions GetFlakeIndexResponse uses, over the same set.<br><br>runs_in_window is the population: archive index keys of this namespace inside the window, every finished status — the count GetStats reports as runs_by_status succeeded + failed + canceled for the same window. Runs still in flight are not in it; they are counted once they finish. |
| `runs_scanned` | `int64` | runs_scanned is how many of those had a body to read; less only for an index row whose body is absent (the crash window between the archive's two writes, which ListRuns already skips). Any other unreadable body fails the call. |
| `runs_dispatched` | `int64` | runs_dispatched is how many scanned runs dispatched at least one task. |
| `runs_evidence_complete` | `int64` | runs_evidence_complete counts dispatched runs holding at least one attempt record for every task they dispatched; runs_evidence_missing counts those holding none for at least one. They sum to runs_dispatched. The consumption of a task with no record is NOT in any sum above: reclaimed on the run's retention schedule, removed by a lifecycle rule, or never written by a best-effort Orker write — the reader cannot tell which, and says "missing". |
| `runs_evidence_missing` | `int64` |  |
| `coverage_since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | coverage_since is the creation time of the OLDEST run in the window that still has at least one attempt record. Runs created before it have none — on a deployment whose cleanup worker reclaims records, that is where reclamation has reached. Unset when no run in the window has a record. runs_evidence_missing counts every run, before or after it, that is missing evidence for some task. |
| `budget` | [`Budget`](#budget) | THE BUDGET. Read from the namespace document on every call — policy is never cached — and held against the measurement above.<br><br>budget is the namespace's budget at the moment of this answer; unset means unbounded. |
| `budget_window` | `bool` | budget_window is true when the answered window is exactly the trailing budget period the admission gate evaluates: the request set neither since nor until, and set lookback equal to budget.period. Only then is a share of the budget meaningful, and only then is budget_reached set. |
| `budget_reached` | `bool` | budget_reached is true when budget_window is true and total has reached any dimension the budget bounds (used ≥ bound). It is the same decision the admission gate makes, so an enforced budget with budget_reached true is one whose next submit is refused, unless the measurement ages out first. A soft budget reports it and refuses nothing. False whenever budget_window is false. |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace, window_since, window_until and computed_at are the question that was answered and when it was measured, exactly as GetStatsResponse carries them. computed_at is the age of the measurement; an answer may be served from a cache of up to ORK_USAGE_CACHE_TTL. |
| `window_since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `window_until` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `computed_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |

### ImagePolicy

ImagePolicy is the deployment's supply-chain floor (AGENTS.md §5): which
images may be applied and executed anywhere in this deployment. It is
stored in the artifact store at metadata/settings/image-policy.json,
beside RetentionPolicy, so any replica answers for it. A deployment that
never wrote one has the empty policy, which permits exactly what today's
behaviour permits.

A namespace may TIGHTEN this policy (Namespace.require_signed_by) and can
never loosen it: there is no namespace field for either floor below.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `require_digest` | `bool` | require_digest refuses a `uses:` written as a mutable tag. The engine already RESOLVES a tag to a digest at apply; this refuses the tag as an INPUT, which is a different and stricter question — "the document must name what it meant", not merely "we recorded what it resolved to". A catalog name (`uses: shell`) is not a tag the author wrote and is exempt; the catalog is the operator's own configuration. |
| `allowed_registries` | repeated `string` | allowed_registries are literal "{registry}/{repository}" prefixes, matched on "/" boundaries against the RESOLVED name (docker.io/library/ alpine, never alpine). Empty means no restriction, which is today's behaviour and what an upgrade preserves. The rule is internal/task.ValidRegistryPrefix and RegistryAllowed, the one place it is implemented; the store refuses an entry that fails it. |
| `signing_keys` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; | signing_keys are the cosign PUBLIC keys a namespace may require by name (Namespace.require_signed_by = "cosign:&lt;name>"): name → PEM "PUBLIC KEY" block, ECDSA P-256, exactly what `cosign generate-key-pair` writes to cosign.pub. Public material only: nothing in OrkStack ever holds or uses a private key. A key a namespace still names cannot be removed (FAILED_PRECONDITION naming the namespace) — the same "lower the namespace first" rule UpdateRetentionPolicy applies. |
| `updated_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | updated_at is written by the store on every write; unset means no policy document has ever been written. |

### ImageRef

ImageRef is an OCI image resolved to an immutable reference. The engine
produces it at apply time and it never changes afterwards: a run executes
what `pinned` names, whatever a tag does later.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `reference` | `string` | reference is what the author wrote, verbatim: "ghcr.io/acme/migrate:v3", "shell", or an already-pinned "repo@sha256:...". Never used to pull. |
| `registry` | `string` | registry is the resolved host, e.g. "ghcr.io" or "docker.io". |
| `repository` | `string` | repository is the resolved path, e.g. "acme/migrate". |
| `index_digest` | `string` | index_digest is the digest of the object the tag named at resolve time: an OCI image index for a multi-platform tag, an image manifest otherwise. Spelled "sha256:&lt;64 hex>". |
| `pinned` | `string` | pinned is the only string that may be pulled or run: "{registry}/{repository}@{index_digest}" |
| `media_type` | `string` | media_type is the media type index_digest addresses. |
| `platforms` | repeated `string` | platforms lists the platforms the index advertises, "os/arch[/variant]". Empty for a single-manifest reference. |
| `platform_digest` | `string` | platform_digest is the manifest digest the Orker actually ran, and the platform it ran on. The engine leaves both empty; only an Orker fills them, and only into ExecuteTaskResult.image and ActivityCommit.image. |
| `platform` | `string` |  |
| `delivery` | `string` | delivery records how the Orker obtained the image for this execution: "registry" (pulled) or "embedded" (loaded from the OCI image layout, §4.6). The engine leaves it empty; only an Orker fills it, beside platform_digest. It exists because objective deliverable 10's embedded fallback is otherwise invisible after the fact: an operator debugging a stale builtin needs to know the pull did not happen. |

### ListAuditRecordsRequest

ListAuditRecordsRequest lists the deployment's audit trail. It is a
deployment-wide listing: a `namespace` filter narrows it like any other
property of a record, and `namespace=` (the empty value) selects the
deployment-wide writes, which carry no namespace
(docs/UI_CLI_PARITY.md "Filtering lists", "Control-plane audit trail").

The window is the `at` interval the filters bound: at &lt; T ends it
(default: the moment the answer is computed, on the engine's clock) and
at >= T starts it (default: seven days before the end). A window whose
end is not after its start is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `page_size` | `int32` | page_size caps the records returned; 0 means the default (50), and a value above the maximum (200) is INVALID_ARGUMENT, not clamped. |
| `page_token` | `string` | page_token continues a listing. It is opaque and versioned, and binds the canonical filter set and the resolved window: a token presented with other filters is INVALID_ARGUMENT. |
| `filters` | repeated [`FieldFilter`](#fieldfilter) |  |

### ListAuditRecordsResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `records` | repeated [`AuditRecord`](#auditrecord) | newest first |
| `next_page_token` | `string` | empty when the window is exhausted |
| `since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | since and until are the window the answer covers, resolved — what a client prints so a reader knows what "the last week" meant on the engine's clock. |
| `until` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |

### ListDeliveriesRequest

ListDeliveriesRequest lists the deployment's delivery records. It is a
deployment-wide listing: a `namespace` filter narrows it to one run
namespace like any other property of a record. Every filterable field is
in the record's key, so a body is read only for a record that matches
(docs/UI_CLI_PARITY.md "Filtering lists", "Webhook deliveries").

The window is the created_at interval the filters bound: created_at &lt; T
ends it (default: the moment the answer is computed) and created_at >= T
starts it (default: the run's created_at when exactly one run_id equals
filter names a run the engine can read, otherwise seven days before the
end). A window whose end is not after its start is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

### LiveAttempt

LiveAttempt is ONE pending ExecuteTask attempt as the cluster sees it now.
It is not durable and is not a record: when the attempt ends the durable
answer is the TaskAttempt record the Orker writes.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `attempt` | `int32` | attempt is Temporal's attempt number for the pending activity (PendingActivityInfo.attempt). While STARTED it is the number the Orker's own record will carry; while SCHEDULED between retries it is the number of the attempt that is ABOUT to run. |
| `state` | [`LiveAttemptState`](#liveattemptstate) |  |
| `attempt_scheduled_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | attempt_scheduled_at is Temporal's scheduled_time for the pending attempt: for a retry, the instant the backoff ends. attempt_started_at is Temporal's last_started_time and is set only while STARTED or CANCEL_REQUESTED. Neither is an Orker clock. |
| `attempt_started_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `next_attempt_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | next_attempt_at is set only while SCHEDULED between attempts: the previous attempt failed and Temporal will start the next one at this time (next_attempt_schedule_time). The previous attempt's error is in ListTaskAttempts, not here. |
| `timeout_seconds` | `int32` | timeout_seconds and cancellation_grace_period_seconds are the task's own bounds as dispatched (ExecuteTaskInput 15 and 16, read from the scheduling event). The Orker arms timeout_seconds when the container is started, AFTER staging and the image pull, so attempt_started_at + timeout_seconds is the EARLIEST the container can be killed, not the moment it will be. A client that prints a remaining time prints a lower bound and says so. |
| `cancellation_grace_period_seconds` | `int32` |  |
| `expires_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | expires_at is Temporal's backstop for this attempt (expiration_time: the StartToClose deadline the engine computed at schedule, OCI contract §6.3). It is deliberately generous and is not the task's timeout. |
| `heartbeat_available` | `bool` | heartbeat_available is true ONLY when state is STARTED or CANCEL_REQUESTED, a heartbeat has arrived since attempt_started_at, and its detail decodes as the Orker's shape. Every field from last_heartbeat_at down is meaningless when it is false and MUST render as unavailable, never as zero or empty. |
| `heartbeat_unavailable_reason` | [`HeartbeatUnavailableReason`](#heartbeatunavailablereason) | heartbeat_unavailable_reason is set exactly when heartbeat_available is false, and UNSPECIFIED when it is true. |
| `last_heartbeat_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | last_heartbeat_at is the cluster's time of the last beat from this attempt (last_heartbeat_time). |
| `heartbeat_stale` | `bool` | heartbeat_stale is computed_at - last_heartbeat_at > task.HeartbeatStaleAfter (two ceiling ticks, 20 s): a healthy Orker beats at least every task.MaxHeartbeatInterval, so an older beat means the Orker is gone, partitioned, or cannot reach the frontend. Temporal has not yet acted: it times the attempt out at heartbeat_deadline_at, after which the attempt is retried or the task fails, and this attempt becomes an UNREPORTED row in ListTaskAttempts if the Orker never files a record. |
| `heartbeat_deadline_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | heartbeat_deadline_at is last_heartbeat_at + the heartbeat timeout (task.HeartbeatTimeout, 30 s): the instant Temporal times this attempt out unless another beat arrives first. Computed here so no client needs to know the constant. |
| `phase` | `string` | phase is the phase the attempt is in, in the Orker's own vocabulary: "start", "commit-check", "workspace", "stage-inputs", "image", "render", "create", "run", "exit", "validate", "commit", "timeout", "cancel"; "image-policy" is entered only when the task carries an image policy (ExecuteTaskInput.image_policy), between "commit-check" and "workspace". Not an enum, for the reason TaskAttempt.phase is a string. |
| `container_id` | `string` | container_id is the runtime's id for the container, once one exists. |
| `bytes_logged` | `int64` | bytes_logged is every byte the workload has written to stdout AND stderr, counted before the per-stream retention cap drops any — so it keeps growing after retention stops. Zero with heartbeat_available true means the workload has written nothing. |
| `orker_id` | `string` | orker_id is the Orker that sent the heartbeat, as it names itself (ORK_ORKER_ID) — the same value TaskRun.orker_id and TaskAttempt.orker_id carry. Empty when the beat came from an Orker built before the detail carried it. |
| `item` | optional `int32` | item is set when the pending activity is one item of a fan-out (read off the scheduled ExecuteTaskInput.each.index). |

### Namespace

Namespace is a tenant of one OrkStack deployment: a scope that owns orkflow
names, runs and pool defaults. Two namespaces may both hold an orkflow
called "deploy" and never see each other's documents.

It is OrkStack's own coordinate. The deployment runtime partition is an
operator setting outside this contract and appears in no proto field, DSL
key, CLI flag or UI control.

The registry lives in the artifact store at metadata/namespaces/{name}.json.
"default" always resolves and is never created: a deployment that registered
nothing still has one namespace, and every orkflow that names none is in it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | name is a slug, unique in the deployment, and is the key of the document. |
| `description` | `string` |  |
| `labels` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; |  |
| `default_pool` | `string` | default_pool is where a task that names no pool runs. Empty means the built-in pool "main".<br><br>It is read on the submit path: a run's routing resolves a task's own `pool:`, then this, then "main". The registry stores only a name the engine can route to — the same slug rule the DSL and the engine's pool mapping use — because a stored routing target nothing can honour is a defect, not a placeholder. |
| `allowed_pools` | repeated `string` | allowed_pools bounds every pool this namespace may dispatch onto. Empty means no restriction. A non-empty list must contain default_pool, which the registry refuses to store otherwise — an allow-list that excludes the namespace's own default would refuse every task that names no pool. Each entry is held to the same pool-name rule as default_pool.<br><br>It is enforced at the API boundary, in both places a pool can be chosen: when an orkflow is applied, with the file in hand, and again when a run is submitted, which is the gate no client can bypass. |
| `created_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | created_at and updated_at are written by the registry, never by a client: created_at when the document is first written and preserved on every later write, updated_at on each one. |
| `updated_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `etag` | `string` | etag is the registry's compare-and-swap token for this document: the value a read handed back, which an update sends back to say which version it edited. A write whose etag no longer matches the stored one is refused, so two operators editing the same namespace at once cannot silently clobber each other — the loser is told to re-read.<br><br>An EMPTY etag is a condition too, not the absence of one: it says the version this update edited had no stored bytes at all, and the write is refused if some other writer has since created them. That is what the default namespace needs — until somebody writes its document a read hands back a synthesized one carrying no token — and it is why an update never has an unconditional mode: an empty token read as "overwrite whatever is there" turned the promise above off for exactly the one namespace every deployment has.<br><br>It is the store's token and opaque: nothing derives meaning from its shape, and a client only ever round-trips it. It is never stored inside the document — it names the document's stored bytes, so a copy inside them could only ever be the token of the write before. |
| `run_retention` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | run_retention is how long a finished run of this namespace stays readable before OrkStack retires it and reclaims its run-scoped storage. Unset means "the deployment maximum" (SystemService.GetRetentionPolicy), which is also the most any namespace may ask for: a value above the maximum is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, and the maximum applies even to a stored value that a later, lower maximum left above it.<br><br>It counts from the moment the run finished, never from submission: a run that executed for two days under a 72h retention is readable for 72h after it ended. Resolution is archive.EffectiveRunRetention, the one place that implements it — the same shape default_pool has in DefaultPoolFor. |
| `telemetry` | [`TelemetryPolicy`](#telemetrypolicy) | telemetry is this namespace's selection among the deployment's telemetry sinks. It names things the operator declared (ORK_TELEMETRY_SINKS) and can never name an endpoint or a credential (AGENTS.md §6): a namespace admin chooses WHERE among the operator's destinations, not the destination itself. Unset means "the default sink, deployment defaults". |
| `hold` | [`NamespaceHold`](#namespacehold) | hold, when set, refuses every new run of this namespace at submit with FAILED_PRECONDITION, naming the reason and since. Unset means accepting, which is what every namespace has today and what an upgrade preserves.<br><br>It is enforced in exactly one place — SubmitRun's preparation, the gate every door into a namespace already goes through (orkctl, the UI, `run again`, a trigger invoke) — and read from the registry on every submit, so a hold set through one replica is honoured by every other on its next request. |
| `max_running` | `int32` | max_running bounds how many runs of this namespace may be in flight at once — accepted and not finished, which is exactly the population GetStatsResponse.running reports. 0 means unlimited, which is the inherited default and what every namespace has today.<br><br>It is evaluated by reading the cluster's execution index at submit — the same read GetStats.running performs (docs/STATS.md §1) — so no OrkStack counter exists to disagree with it tomorrow. That makes it best-effort under simultaneous submits against several replicas: each reads, then acts, with no lock between, and the overshoot is bounded by the number of submits racing through the window between one replica's read and the cluster indexing its start. A lock would remove the overshoot and AGENTS.md §2.1 forbids building one, which is the right trade — a guard that is occasionally one over is worth far more than a lock service. A namespace that sets 0 never pays the read at all. |
| `allowed_secrets` | repeated `string` | allowed_secrets bounds which SecretRef.source values a task of this namespace may resolve. Empty means UNRESTRICTED, which is what every namespace has today and therefore what an upgrade preserves — a deployment that sets none behaves exactly as it did before this field existed. It bounds NAMES: nothing that reads this field stores, compares or transmits a secret value.<br><br>Each entry is `scheme:pattern`. The scheme is literal. The pattern is matched against the locator ONLY, never across the separator, and never as a regular expression: "*" is the one wildcard and it does not cross "/"; every other character is itself. A "file:" locator with a ".." segment is refused outright rather than normalized, so a pattern cannot be escaped by path traversal. The rule is internal/dsl.ValidSecretPattern and CheckSecretSource, the one place it is implemented; the registry refuses an entry that fails it.<br><br>It is enforced at the API boundary in the two places a secret can be named, exactly as allowed_pools is: when an orkflow is applied or validated, with the file in hand (an issue anchored to tasks[i].secrets[j].source), and again when a run is submitted, which is the gate no client can bypass and which catches a definition stored while the list was wider. It composes by INTERSECTION with each Orker's own floor (ORK_ORKER_SECRET_ALLOW): a namespace can only ever narrow what its Orkers already permit. |
| `require_signed_by` | `string` | require_signed_by names a signer every image executed in this namespace must satisfy: "cosign:&lt;key-name>", where &lt;key-name> is one of the deployment's ImagePolicy.signing_keys. Unset means no signature is required, which is what every namespace has today and what an upgrade preserves. A namespace may only TIGHTEN the deployment policy: this is its one field for doing so, and there is none for loosening.<br><br>It is enforced in the three places an image passes: at apply and validate, with the file in hand (a field-anchored issue on tasks[i].uses); at submit, before a run id is minted, which catches a definition stored before the requirement existed; and by the Orker at dispatch, which verifies the signature itself against the key the run pinned at submit. Only "cosign:" exists; it is a closed set, not an extension point (AGENTS.md §13). |
| `budget` | [`Budget`](#budget) | budget bounds this namespace's reserved consumption over a rolling period. Unset means unbounded, which is what every namespace has today and what an upgrade preserves.<br><br>An enforced budget is checked in exactly one place — the admission gate in SubmitRun's preparation, after the hold and max_running — by reading the namespace's usage over the trailing period. That read is a read-then-act with no lock, cached for at most ORK_USAGE_CACHE_TTL, and counts a run only once it has finished, so enforcement is best-effort by a bounded margin: the runs that finished inside one cache lifetime, every run still in flight, and submits racing the check. A lock would remove the margin and AGENTS.md §2.1 forbids building one. |

### NamespaceHold

NamespaceHold stops this namespace ACCEPTING new runs. It is an admission
decision and never a retroactive one: a run already accepted continues, is
readable, and finishes normally (AGENTS.md §15). Releasing a hold starts
nothing that was refused while it was set — a refused submit was refused,
not queued.

It is a message rather than two scalars on Namespace so that "held" is one
presence check (hold != nil) and a hold can never be half-set.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | `string` | reason is required. A hold with no reason is refused by the registry: the next operator to read this document is the one who has to decide whether to release it, and "on hold" with no why is not a decision they can make. It is a short human line, bounded at 512 bytes with no control characters, never a secret and never machine-parsed. |
| `since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | since is written by the registry on the write that SET the hold and preserved on every later write while it stays set, never supplied by a client — the same rule created_at/updated_at follow. Editing the reason of a hold does not move it: the door has been closed since the first write, whatever the sign on it now says. |

### OpSchema

OpSchema is the key set one `op` reads, beside the shared `fields`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fields` | map&lt;`string`, [`FieldSchema`](#fieldschema)&gt; |  |

### OpenPin

OpenPin is one pin this Orker currently hosts: a pin it has accepted and
not yet closed. It names the run and the pin, never the mechanism behind
it (AGENTS.md §7), and says when the shared directory's
lease ends, which is the longest the pin can live even if nothing else
closes it (docs/OCI_ACTIVITY_CONTRACT.md §6.4).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `string` |  |
| `pin` | `string` | pin is the name the author wrote in `pin:`. EMPTY until the pin's first member attempt arrives: the Orker learns the name from ExecuteTaskInput.pin, and a pin is open from the moment it is accepted, before any member has been dispatched to it. |
| `since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | since is when this Orker accepted the pin. |
| `expires_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | expires_at is the shared directory's lease (lease.json). UNSET until the first member arrives and writes it; a client renders "-", never a time. |

### Orker

Orker is one execution process, observed live.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orker_id` | `string` |  |
| `pool` | `string` | pool is the pool the Orker reports serving (DescribeOrkerResult.pool). |
| `build_id` | `string` | empty when versioning is off |
| `running_tasks` | `int32` |  |
| `open_pins` | `int32` |  |
| `max_concurrent_pins` | `int32` | ORK_ORKER_MAX_PINS; 0 means not a pin host |
| `cordoned` | `bool` |  |
| `cordon_reason` | `string` | empty when not cordoned |
| `cordoned_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `last_seen` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | last_seen is the most recent moment this Orker was observed polling. It answers "how fresh is this row", never "when did this Orker die". |
| `unavailable_reason` | `string` | unavailable_reason says this Orker COULD NOT BE ASKED, and why — the same three-state distinction Pool.unavailable_reason makes, for the same reason: "not measured" rendered as "measured zero" sends an operator to stop a host that may be mid-task. When set, fields 2–9 and 12 are unset: nothing was measured, so there is no number to report. |
| `pins` | repeated [`OpenPin`](#openpin) |  |
| `capacity` | [`ResourceQuantity`](#resourcequantity) | capacity and reserved are DescribeOrkerResult's: what this Orker admits tasks within, and what stands reserved against it, each outstanding poll counted at the per-task cap. Both unset when it declares no capacity. |
| `reserved` | [`ResourceQuantity`](#resourcequantity) |  |
| `max_request` | [`ResourceQuantity`](#resourcequantity) | max_request is DescribeOrkerResult's: the per-task cap, the largest request this Orker runs, which submit holds a task's declared request to. |

### Orkflow

Orkflow is the compiled, validated form of a DSL document.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | unique identifier (slug) |
| `version` | `string` | semantic or content hash |
| `description` | `string` |  |
| `labels` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; |  |
| `inputs` | `google.protobuf.Struct` | inputs declares the accepted input parameters (JSON schema fragment as struct). |
| `tasks` | repeated [`Task`](#task) |  |
| `source_yaml` | `string` | original DSL for round-trip/audit |
| `created_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace scopes this orkflow. Empty means the built-in "default" namespace. A name is unique WITHIN a namespace, never globally: two namespaces may both hold an orkflow called "deploy", and they are two different orkflows stored under two different keys. |
| `definition_digest` | `string` | definition_digest is the canonical digest of THIS document's definition (§4.4): "sha256:" + hex(sha256(canonicalOrkflow(wf))).<br><br>It is computed at APPLY, after image resolution, and stamped here — "the version document is the pin", which is what AGENTS.md §7.2 requires of a run. Workflow code READS it and never computes it, so a run records the digest of the definition it actually pinned rather than one derived from whatever a later reader happened to reconstruct.<br><br>It is NOT part of canonicalOrkflow. The canonical form enumerates its fields and this one is not among them, so stamping the digest into the document it describes does not change that digest: the value is stable under re-canonicalization, and pkg/artifacts.sameStoredOrkflow still sees a re-apply of an unchanged document as equal.<br><br>Added after the original wire freeze, deliberately and ADDITIVELY: fields 1-9 are untouched, so `buf breaking` WIRE and WIRE_JSON stay clean and an older reader simply does not see it. The alternative was to populate orkflow_definition_digest from workflow code, which changes recorded activity-payload bytes and would force re-recording the base replay fixture, which is never re-recorded. |
| `pins` | repeated [`Pin`](#pin) | pins declares every Pin a task may name, sorted by name at compile so one document always compiles to one message. Part of canonicalOrkflow, emitted ONLY when non-empty (see Task.pin). |
| `outputs` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; | outputs is this Orkflow's declared return contract: output name to a template over .inputs and .tasks.&lt;id>.output, rendered ONCE, by the engine, when a run succeeds; every value renders to a string. When non-empty the rendered map IS Run.output, and is what a composing parent's task receives as its values. When empty, Run.output keeps the leaf aggregation it has always had, and a composing parent's task receives {}. Part of canonicalOrkflow only when non-empty (see pins). |

### OrkflowCaller

OrkflowCaller is one reference to an orkflow. Fields marked with a kind
are set only for that kind.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | [`OrkflowCallerKind`](#orkflowcallerkind) |  |
| `name` | `string` | name is the composing orkflow's name (ORKFLOW), the schedule's name (SCHEDULE), or the trigger's optional name (TRIGGER; may be empty). |
| `id` | `string` | id is the trigger's or the schedule's opaque id; empty for ORKFLOW. |
| `caller_version` | `string` | ORKFLOW: the composing version, whether it is that orkflow's resolved current version, and the composed task. |
| `caller_version_is_current` | `bool` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `pinned_version` | `string` | pinned_version is the version of THIS orkflow the caller starts. Always set for ORKFLOW. Empty for a trigger or schedule that follows the current pointer — or, for a SCHEDULE, when unavailable_reason is set, in which case it is UNKNOWN, not "follows current". |
| `pinned_definition_digest` | `string` | ORKFLOW: the definition digest the composing version pinned. |
| `outputs_read` | repeated `string` | ORKFLOW: the output names of this orkflow the composing version's templates read through the composed task (with:, condition:, outputs:), sorted and distinct. |
| `inputs_supplied` | repeated `string` | ORKFLOW: the top-level keys of the composed task's with: — the inputs it supplies — sorted. |
| `description` | `string` | TRIGGER, SCHEDULE: the operator's description, verbatim. |
| `unavailable_reason` | `string` | SCHEDULE: set when the cluster did not describe the schedule for this read, so the version it pins is not known. Never a guess. |

### OrkflowFailures

OrkflowFailures is one orkflow's failure record inside the window: how many
of its finished runs failed, and how many finished at all.

Both numbers travel together because neither means anything alone. Three
failures out of four is an outage; three out of three thousand is Tuesday.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` |  |
| `failed` | `int64` |  |
| `total` | `int64` |  |

### OrkflowRef

OrkflowRef names one immutable Orkflow version in the referencing
definition's OWN namespace — a composition never crosses a namespace.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `version` | `string` |  |
| `definition_digest` | `string` | definition_digest is the referenced version's Orkflow.definition_digest, stamped at apply. Empty only in a message the compiler produced before internal/api resolved it; a stored definition never carries an empty one. |

### OrkflowVersion

OrkflowVersion is one stored version in a version listing: the document's
coordinates, not the document.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `string` |  |
| `applied_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `is_current` | `bool` | is_current marks the version an empty version resolves to — the pointer's target when one is set, otherwise the most recently applied version. |
| `description` | `string` |  |
| `interface_verdict` | [`InterfaceVerdict`](#interfaceverdict) | interface_verdict is this version's declared interface compared with the version marked is_current — "what would promoting this version break" (CompareInterfaces with from = current, to = this). UNSPECIFIED on the is_current row itself. Computed on read from documents the listing already reads; stored nowhere. |

### PendingOrkflow

PendingOrkflow is an orkflow version the same client invocation applies
BEFORE it executes this plan (an orkflow document beside the automation
document). The planner treats a reference to it as satisfied.

### PhaseSpan

PhaseSpan is one §7.1 phase of one attempt, on the Orker's clock. Spans
are recorded by the dispatcher's own Phase() sequence, so a list of them is
contiguous: each span's finished_at is the next span's started_at, the
first begins at the attempt's first Phase call, and the last ends at
TaskAttempt.finished_at. The names are the dispatcher's own — "start",
"commit-check", "workspace", "stage-inputs", "image", "render", "create",
"run", "exit", "validate", "commit", and, entered from the wait path,
"timeout" and "cancel"; "image-policy" is entered only when the task
carries an image policy (ExecuteTaskInput.image_policy), between
"commit-check" and "workspace"; "memo" and "stage-artifacts" are entered
only by an attempt of a cached task, after "stage-inputs" — and are not an enum, for the reason
TaskAttempt.phase is a string: a reader of an older build must be able to
read a phase it has never heard of.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `phase` | `string` |  |
| `started_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `finished_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |

### Pin

Pin is a named group of tasks that execute on ONE Orker process and share
/orkstack/shared for the group's lifetime (docs/DSL.md "Pins"). What
implements it is internal, as a pool's routing is (AGENTS.md §7).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | slug, unique within the orkflow |
| `timeout_seconds` | `int32` | timeout_seconds bounds the whole pin, from the moment its first task is dispatched until its last task ends. 0 means derived: the sum of every member task's wall-clock budget, which is the sequential worst case. |

### PlanAutomationRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `yaml` | `string` | the automation document, as read |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace, when non-empty, must EQUAL the document's `namespace:`; a mismatch is an issue on `namespace`, never a silent choice. A client sends it only when its user named a namespace explicitly (docs/AUTOMATION.md). |
| `prune` | `bool` | prune turns every undeclared named object of a managed section into a DELETE step. |
| `pending_orkflows` | repeated [`PendingOrkflow`](#pendingorkflow) |  |

### PlanAutomationResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace is the document's namespace, resolved ("default" spelled out). |
| `managed` | repeated [`AutomationObjectKind`](#automationobjectkind) | managed lists the sections the document declares, in the order NAMESPACE (settings), SCHEDULE, TRIGGER, WEBHOOK. |
| `steps` | repeated [`AutomationStep`](#automationstep) | steps, in execution order (docs/AUTOMATION.md "Step order"): actionable steps first — namespace, creates, updates, deletes — then the rest. |
| `issues` | repeated [`ValidationIssue`](#validationissue) | issues: any ERROR means no step may be executed, and every client refuses to execute any. A document that failed to parse has issues and no steps. |
| `plan_digest` | `string` | plan_digest is "sha256:&lt;64 lowercase hex>" over the namespace and the actionable steps (action, kind, name, id, changes) — what a reviewer pins with `orkctl apply --expect-plan`. It excludes the carried requests, so a no-op rewrite of the namespace (a new etag) does not move it; it excludes UNCHANGED, UNDECLARED and UNMANAGED steps, which write nothing. Defined even when nothing is actionable ("no changes" is pinnable); empty exactly when nothing was planned (the document did not parse, or names another namespace than the request). |

### PlanRunRequest

PlanRunRequest names ONE definition, one input, and optional stub outputs.

Exactly one of orkflow_name and yaml is set. With orkflow_name, the
definition is the stored version the three coordinates address, resolved
exactly as GetOrkflow and SubmitRun resolve it (empty version = the
current pointer). With yaml, the definition is prepared from the document
exactly as ValidateOrkflow prepares it — compiled against the deployment's
activity catalog, namespace-checked, images resolved, digest computed —
and stored nowhere.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` |  |
| `orkflow_version` | `string` | empty = the current pointer |
| `namespace` | `string` | empty = the default namespace |
| `input` | [`Payload`](#payload) | input is the run input exactly as SubmitRunRequest.input would carry it; the definition's declared defaults fill omitted keys, caller keys always win. The effective, defaulted input is echoed on the response. |
| `assumed_outputs` | map&lt;`string`, [`Payload`](#payload)&gt; | assumed_outputs stubs the values.json of a task that would run, keyed by task id, so a downstream condition that reads .tasks.&lt;id>.output.&lt;field> can be planned both ways. A key that is not a task id of the definition is InvalidArgument naming it. A task that runs with no entry here is planned with an EMPTY output map — which is exactly what the interpreter gives a condition when the upstream wrote no such field — and every task whose condition read such an output is listed in PlanTask.assumed_absent. An entry for a task that does not run is reported in unused_assumed_outputs, never silently dropped. |
| `yaml` | `string` | yaml is an unapplied document to plan instead of a stored version. It is prepared, not stored: the same function ValidateOrkflow uses, with the same errors. namespace, when set, must agree with the document's own `namespace:` on the same rule ApplyOrkflow applies. |
| `assume_failed` | repeated `string` | assume_failed plans the run as if each named task, when it would run, FAILED after its retries: its failure handlers are planned, every task that is not a failure handler and transitively needs it is UNREACHED, and work that does not depend on it is planned as if nothing had failed (in a run it may be canceled in flight). Each entry is a task id of the definition, at most once; an unknown or repeated id is InvalidArgument naming it. An entry whose task does not run is reported in unused_assume_failed. |

### PlanRunResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` | The definition that was planned: the coordinates and the digest of the exact document, so a plan of a pinned version and a plan of `current` can be told apart after the pointer moves. |
| `orkflow_version` | `string` |  |
| `namespace` | `string` |  |
| `definition_digest` | `string` |  |
| `from_yaml` | `bool` | from_yaml is true when the request planned an unapplied document; the version is then whatever the document pins or the derived source hash, and nothing under these coordinates is stored. |
| `input` | [`Payload`](#payload) | input is the EFFECTIVE input: the request's, with declared defaults applied, exactly what RunWorkflow would see as .inputs. |
| `tasks` | repeated [`PlanTask`](#plantask) | declaration order |
| `waves` | repeated [`PlanWave`](#planwave) | 1..wave_count, RUNS tasks only |
| `runs` | `int32` | count of RUNS |
| `skipped` | `int32` | count of SKIPPED |
| `wave_count` | `int32` | wave_count is the highest wave of any RUNS task; 0 when nothing runs. |
| `unused_assumed_outputs` | repeated `string` | unused_assumed_outputs lists request keys whose task did not RUN, in sorted order: the stub was accepted and had no effect. |
| `awaits` | `int32` | count of AWAITS |
| `assumed_failed` | `int32` | count of ASSUMED_FAILED |
| `unused_assume_failed` | repeated `string` | unused_assume_failed lists request entries whose task is not ASSUMED_FAILED (it was SKIPPED or UNREACHED), in request order. |
| `fails_at` | `string` | fails_at is the task at which the planned run starts failing — the first FAILS or ASSUMED_FAILED in decision order — or empty when nothing fails. The run is planned FAILED exactly when it is set; each UNREACHED task names its own cause in PlanTask.unreached_by. |

### PlanTask

PlanTask is one task's planned outcome. Tasks are listed in declaration
order, the order readyTasks scans them in.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `outcome` | [`PlanOutcome`](#planoutcome) |  |
| `wave` | `int32` | wave is the dispatch depth: 1 for a task with no needs, otherwise one more than the highest wave among its needs. A SKIPPED task carries the wave it WOULD have been dispatched in, so a reader sees where in the graph the branch closed; it is not counted in PlanRunResponse.wave_count because a skip costs the interpreter no activity and no wait. 0 for FAILS and UNREACHED.<br><br>A wave is a depth, not a clock: the interpreter re-scans after EVERY completion, so with real durations a wave-3 task may start before a slower wave-2 task on another branch finishes. wave_count is the minimum number of sequential dispatch rounds, which is what an author asking "how parallel is this" wants to know. |
| `skip_reason` | `string` | skip_reason is, for SKIPPED, the exact sentence the interpreter logs after "task skipped: " — `upstream task "<id>" was skipped` or `condition "<expression>" evaluated false`. Empty otherwise. |
| `skipped_by` | `string` | skipped_by is, for an upstream skip, the id of the need that caused it (the first skipped entry of `needs:`, as classify finds it). Empty for a condition skip and for every other outcome. |
| `condition` | `string` | condition is the task's `condition:` as written, empty when it has none. |
| `pin` | `string` | pin is the task's `pin:` as written, empty when unpinned. Rendered so a reader sees which RUNS tasks would open and share a pin; a pin whose every member is SKIPPED is never opened by the interpreter and is rendered as such. |
| `assumed_absent` | repeated `string` | assumed_absent lists the upstream task ids this task's condition reads through .tasks.&lt;id> for which the request supplied no assumed output, in sorted order. Those outputs were planned as {}. Set only when the condition was actually evaluated (RUNS, or SKIPPED by its condition); empty for an upstream skip, FAILS, and UNREACHED. |
| `error` | [`Error`](#error) | error is set for FAILS and ASSUMED_FAILED: for the task at fails_at, the error the interpreter records on the RUN (code RUN_FAILED for a condition error, ASSUMED_FAILED for an assumption); for any later FAILS, the error recorded on that task (code CONDITION_FAILED). |
| `await` | [`AwaitSpec`](#awaitspec) | await is the task's AwaitSpec, set for an awaited task whatever its outcome, so a reader sees the deadline and whether it takes a callback. |
| `each` | [`EachSpec`](#eachspec) | each is the task's EachSpec, set for a fan-out whatever its outcome. |
| `each_count` | optional `int32` | each_count is the number of items the plan can already count: set when the source is an input, or a task whose values assumed_outputs stubs; unset when the count is a run-time fact. |
| `orkflow` | [`OrkflowRef`](#orkflowref) | orkflow is the task's Task.orkflow, set for a composed task whatever its outcome. A plan never recurses into the child: its input is rendered at run time and its own plan is one more PlanRun call. |
| `cache` | [`CacheSpec`](#cachespec) | cache is the task's CacheSpec, set for a cached task whatever its outcome. A plan never predicts a hit: that is decided on the Orker, from the rendered config and the input digests, when the run reaches it. |
| `join` | [`JoinPolicy`](#joinpolicy) | join is the task's join policy, set whatever its outcome when the definition declares one other than all_succeeded. |
| `unreached_by` | `string` | unreached_by is, for UNREACHED, the task whose failure leaves this one unreached: the first decision-time failure (a FAILS) decided before it, or else the first ASSUMED_FAILED task of its needs closure in declaration order. Empty for every other outcome. |

### PlanWave

PlanWave lists the RUNS, AWAITS and ASSUMED_FAILED tasks of one wave, in
declaration order. There is one entry per wave from 1 to wave_count;
SKIPPED tasks are not members.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `wave` | `int32` |  |
| `task_ids` | repeated `string` |  |

### Pool

Pool is a set of Orkers, observed live.

Nothing writes a Pool: it is derived on read from what the cluster reports
about the Orkers polling for a pool's work, so any replica answers, including
one that started nothing and holds no state of its own.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | name is the pool a task's `pool:` names. "main" is built in and is where a task runs when neither it nor its namespace names one. |
| `live_orker_count` | `int32` | live_orker_count is how many Orkers were serving this pool when the answer was computed. Zero means a task sent here would wait for an Orker that is not there, which is what a submit refuses. |
| `is_default` | `bool` | is_default marks the pool a task of this namespace runs on when it names none. |
| `last_seen` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | last_seen is the most recent moment an Orker of this pool was observed STILL POLLING.<br><br>Temporal remembers a poller for minutes after its worker died, so the probe drops a record older than the freshness window before counting or timestamping anything (internal/engine/pool_probe.go). One consequence is load-bearing and stated here rather than discovered: a pool whose Orkers have all gone quiet reports NO last_seen at all, not the moment the last of them was heard. This field answers "how fresh is the number beside it", never "when did this pool die". |
| `unavailable_reason` | `string` | unavailable_reason says that this pool COULD NOT BE ASKED, and why.<br><br>Empty is the normal case: live_orker_count is a measurement. Non-empty means nothing was measured — the cluster did not answer for this pool — and live_orker_count is 0 because there is no number to report, NOT because nobody is serving it. The two need opposite reactions: an empty pool is fixed by starting an Orker, an unreachable one by asking again, and a renderer that showed them alike would tell an operator to scale a pool that may be perfectly healthy.<br><br>It exists so that ListPools can NARROW instead of refusing. One pool the cluster could not answer for used to fail the whole call, hiding every healthy pool beside it — and an admin read is opened precisely when something is already wrong. Each pool carries its own verdict now. |

### Release

Release is one build of OrkStack — `ork` and `orker` released together
(AGENTS.md §7.2) — as the cluster routes it. No field names the cluster's
own objects or a version's routing internals: a release is OrkStack's word,
as a pool and a pin are (§7.1).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `build_id` | `string` | build_id is the release's identity: the ORK_BUILD_ID its binaries run with. It is the value Orker.build_id and TaskAttempt.build_id carry. |
| `role` | [`ReleaseRole`](#releaserole) |  |
| `ramp_percent` | `float` | ramp_percent is the share of new runs a RAMPING release takes, 0–100, as the cluster holds it (a value set outside OrkStack may be fractional). 0 for every other role. |
| `role_since` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | role_since is when the release became CURRENT or started RAMPING; unset for PREVIOUS and CANDIDATE. |
| `first_seen_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | first_seen_at is when the cluster first saw a process of this release. |
| `engine_replicas` | `int32` | engine_replicas is how many engine processes of this release are live now: distinct processes polling for runs within the freshness window. Always measured — a cluster that cannot answer fails the whole read. |
| `orkers` | repeated [`Orker`](#orker) | orkers are the Orker inventory's rows whose build_id is this release, exactly as ActivityService.ListOrkers returns them (pool, cordon, load, open pins), in that RPC's order. An Orker that did not answer has no build_id and is in ListReleasesResponse.unattributed_orkers instead. |
| `pools_served` | repeated `string` | pools_served is every pool with at least one ANSWERED, UNCORDONED Orker of this release, sorted. A cordoned Orker takes no new task and serves nothing. |
| `runs_in_flight` | `int32` | runs_in_flight is how many runs are executing on this release now, counted by the cluster's run index. Meaningful only when runs_unavailable_reason is empty; otherwise it is 0 and MUST be rendered as unknown, never as zero. |
| `runs_unavailable_reason` | `string` | runs_unavailable_reason says the run index could not be asked, in OrkStack's words. The cluster's own text is logged, never forwarded. |
| `runs` | repeated [`Run`](#run) | runs are up to ten of those runs, newest first, as shallow projections — the fields ListRuns fills from the index (id, namespace, orkflow_name, orkflow_version, status, created_at). Deployment-wide: runs of every namespace, each carrying its own. |
| `drain_state` | [`ReleaseDrainState`](#releasedrainstate) |  |
| `drain_checked_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | drain_checked_at is when the cluster last evaluated drain_state; unset when it has not, or drain_state is UNSPECIFIED. |
| `drained` | `bool` | drained is the one condition under which this release's processes may be stopped: PREVIOUS with drain_state DRAINED (or a CANDIDATE with no runs), no run counted in flight, no open pin on any of its Orkers, and an Orker inventory in which every Orker answered. `orkctl release wait` exits 0 on it and on nothing else. |
| `blockers` | repeated [`ReleaseBlocker`](#releaseblocker) | blockers are every reason this release may not take new runs now, in a stable order. Always empty for CURRENT. Empty for any other role means RampRelease and PromoteRelease would pass their check at the moment of this read. |

### ReservedResources

ReservedResources is what an Orker granted one attempt: the cpu and memory
limits its container was (or, for an attempt that ended before a
container existed, would have been) created with, AFTER the Orker's
defaults filled a missing request and its caps admitted it
(ORK_ORKER_DEFAULT_CPU/_MEMORY, ORK_ORKER_MAX_CPU/_MEMORY). They are the
same values the attempt's task.json reports as resources, as numbers.

A reservation is a limit, not a measurement: nothing here says how much
of it the workload used.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `double` | cpu is the cpu limit in cores: "2" is 2, "500m" is 0.5. |
| `memory_bytes` | `int64` | memory_bytes is the memory limit in bytes: "4Gi" is 4294967296. |

| `task_runs` | repeated [`TaskRun`](#taskrun) |  |

It is present on every snapshot the run writes, on the archived run, and therefore in every webhook payload's embedded run. |
