### RunFieldDiff

RunFieldDiff is one field of one task (or of the run, when task_id is
empty) whose two values differ, or whose evidence is missing on at least
one side. A field that is equal and available on both sides has no row.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `task_id` | `string` | empty for a run-level field |
| `field` | `string` | field is one of: "definition" (run-level); "presence", "status", "attempt", "pool", "pin", "orker", "exit_code", "error", "duration", "image", "platform_digest" (task-level). It is a string, not an enum, so a later contract can add a field a client of this build has never heard of and the client still prints the row. |
| `from_value` | `string` | from_value / to_value are RENDERED strings. Empty with the side available means "does not apply" or "no value" (an unpinned task's pin, a skipped task's exit code); a client prints "-". Empty with the side unavailable means the evidence is gone; a client prints "unavailable" and the reason. |
| `to_value` | `string` |  |
| `from_available` | `bool` |  |
| `to_available` | `bool` |  |
| `from_reason` | `string` | from_reason / to_reason are set only when the side is unavailable: a stable machine token from the list in docs/UI_CLI_PARITY.md ("Run diff"), e.g. "attempt_record_missing", "definition_unavailable", "no_attempt_store". A client renders the token's documented sentence. |
| `to_reason` | `string` |  |
| `item` | optional `int32` | item is set on a row that compares one item of a fan-out task in both runs. |

### RunOrigin

RunOrigin is the immutable record of what started a run. It is decided
once, at submit, by the process that accepted the submission, and travels
on the replay-pinned plan exactly as the definition digest and the
telemetry selection do (internal/engine/plan.go): recorded in history,
identical on every replay, readable by any replica. It records; nothing
in OrkStack reads it to decide anything.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | [`RunOriginKind`](#runoriginkind) |  |
| `id` | `string` | id names the originating object for the kinds that have one — a trigger id, a schedule id, a parent run id, a source run id — and is empty for SUBMIT. Opaque: nothing parses it or derives anything from its shape (AGENTS.md §7). |
| `reference` | `string` | reference is caller-supplied correlation text — a CI job URL, a ticket key, a partner event id — carried through from SubmitRunRequest.origin_reference or the Ork-Origin-Reference header on the trigger door. At most 256 bytes and no control characters, VALIDATED at the request boundary and never sanitized (AGENTS.md §7): an over-long or malformed reference is INVALID_ARGUMENT and starts no run. Opaque to OrkStack: it is never an expression, a selector or a routing key. A client renders it as a link only when it parses as an http(s) URL, and as text otherwise. |
| `description` | `string` | description is the originating object's own human label at the moment of submit — Trigger.description for TRIGGER, the schedule's name for SCHEDULE — copied so a run stays explainable after the trigger is deleted. Empty for SUBMIT, RUN_AGAIN and PARENT_RUN. Bounded to 256 bytes by truncation. |
| `principal` | `string` | principal is what the deployment's gateway asserted in the Ork-Principal request header on the submitting request — the trigger invoke, the Connect SubmitRun — recorded verbatim, bounded to 256 bytes by truncation, and NEVER authenticated: it is the same assertion, on the same terms, as AuditRecord.principal. Empty when no header was present; a client then omits the line entirely rather than showing a blank that could be mistaken for a name. |

### Schedule

Schedule is one schedule as a client sees it: the authored coordinates and
the cluster's live state, merged for this one read and never stored.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | id is opaque, shaped sch-{16 hex}, generated as trg-{16 hex} is (8 bytes from crypto/rand). It is what RunOrigin.id carries for a scheduled run. Nothing parses it or derives anything from its shape. It survives an update and changes on delete-then-create, so `run list --filter origin.kind=SCHEDULE --filter origin.id=<id>` names one schedule's lifetime. |
| `name` | `string` | name is the operator's handle: a slug (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, at most 200 bytes), unique within the namespace, immutable. Every request addresses a schedule by (namespace, name). |
| `namespace` | `string` |  |
| `orkflow_name` | `string` | orkflow_name is the orkflow every fire starts. Immutable. |
| `orkflow_version` | `string` | orkflow_version pins a version; empty means the current pointer, resolved at EACH fire, exactly as SubmitRunRequest.orkflow_version and Trigger.orkflow_version default. A pinned version that no longer exists refuses the fire naming it; it never falls through to current. |
| `input` | [`Payload`](#payload) | input is the JSON object every fire submits, verbatim; the orkflow's declared defaults apply as they do for any submission. Unset is none. |
| `description` | `string` | description is an optional operator label, at most 256 bytes, no control characters. It is NOT what a run's origin shows — that is name — so a label can change without rewriting history's meaning. |
| `spec` | [`ScheduleSpec`](#schedulespec) | spec is the authored schedule spec, exactly as the last create or update sent it, except that an UNSPECIFIED overlap was recorded as SKIP. |
| `paused` | `bool` | paused and note are the cluster's state. note is the pause reason an operator gave, or the text the cluster wrote when pause_on_failure paused it; it is empty when the schedule is not paused and nothing wrote one. |
| `note` | `string` |  |
| `next_fire_times` | repeated `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | next_fire_times is up to the next 10 nominal fire times, read from the cluster for this call; a paused schedule lists the times it would fire at, which is what creating one paused is for. Never stored by OrkStack. |
| `recent_fires` | repeated [`ScheduleFire`](#schedulefire) | recent_fires is up to the last 10 fires, oldest first, read from the cluster for this call. Never stored by OrkStack. |
| `fires_taken` | `int64` | Counters the cluster keeps: fires taken, fires skipped by an overlap policy of SKIP, and fires missed because they fell outside the catch-up window. Read for this call. |
| `fires_skipped_overlap` | `int64` |  |
| `fires_missed_catchup` | `int64` |  |
| `created_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `updated_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `unavailable_reason` | `string` | unavailable_reason is set on a LIST row whose live state the cluster did not answer for. The identity fields (1–4) are then from the list entry and fields 5–17 are unset — never zero, never a guess. A GetSchedule that cannot describe is an error instead, because it would have nothing to return. |

### ScheduleFire

ScheduleFire is one fire of a schedule as the cluster and the fire's own
record describe it. Exactly one of run_id and refusal is set once the fire
has prepared; neither is set while it is still preparing; details_available
is false when the fire could not be described at all (retired past the
cluster's execution retention, or the cluster did not answer), in which
case a client renders "unavailable", never a blank that reads as success.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scheduled_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | scheduled_at is the nominal fire time, jitter included. It is also the started run's origin.reference, in RFC 3339 UTC. |
| `actual_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | actual_at is when the cluster took the action. |
| `run_id` | `string` | run_id is the run this fire started, once known. The run's own status is a run read (GetRun); this record does not repeat it. |
| `refusal` | `string` | refusal is why this fire started no run: the ordinary submit refusal, e.g. `orkflow "reconcile" version "3" in namespace "payments" not found` or `pool "gpu" has no live Orker`. |
| `details_available` | `bool` |  |

### ScheduleSpec

ScheduleSpec is WHEN a schedule fires, as the operator authored it. It is
stored verbatim inside the Temporal Schedule (ScheduleRecord.spec) and is
what every read returns; the cluster compiles cron expressions into its
own calendar form and does not hand the text back, which is why the
authored text travels with the record.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cron` | repeated `string` | cron is zero or more cron expressions; the schedule fires at the union of their times and of interval's. 5, 6 or 7 fields, or @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly, or "@every 15m", as Temporal accepts them. A CRON_TZ= or TZ= prefix is refused: set timezone instead, so one field says which zone the schedule keeps. |
| `interval` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | interval fires every interval, aligned to the Unix epoch (Temporal's ScheduleIntervalSpec with no offset): every 1h fires on the hour, every 15m at :00, :15, :30, :45 — not "15m after creation". |
| `timezone` | `string` | timezone is the IANA zone cron is evaluated in. Empty is UTC. Calendar matching is literal clock time with no DST special-casing, as Temporal documents: a 02:30 fire does not happen on the day that has no 02:30 and happens twice on the day that has two 01:30s. |
| `jitter` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | jitter delays each fire by a uniform random amount in [0, jitter], never past the next fire. Zero is none. |
| `start_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | start_at and end_at bound the fires, inclusive. Unset is unbounded. A spec with no fire left after now is refused, because the cluster retires a schedule with nothing left to do after a few days and the operator would find it gone. |
| `end_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `overlap` | [`OverlapPolicy`](#overlappolicy) | overlap is the policy for a fire that is due while an earlier run of this schedule is still executing. UNSPECIFIED on a create or update is RECORDED as SKIP by the API before anything is written, so every read returns SKIP and never UNSPECIFIED. |
| `catchup_window` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | catchup_window is how late a fire missed while the cluster was down may still be taken once it is back. Unset leaves Temporal's default (one year at the SDK version pinned in go.mod); set, it must be at least 10s, the cluster's minimum. A short window is how a nightly job says "if I could not run last night, do not run at 09:00 when Temporal comes back". |
| `pause_on_failure` | `bool` | pause_on_failure pauses the schedule when a fire ends in failure — a run that failed, or a fire that was refused — so a broken nightly does not fail five nights in a row unobserved. The cluster writes why into the note. Default false. |

### SecretRef

SecretRef names a secret and where the Orker gets it. The value never
appears in a proto message, in Temporal history, or in the archive.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | name is the file name the workload reads under /orkstack/input/secrets/. Validated: ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$. |
| `source` | `string` | source is an Orker-resolvable locator, e.g. "env:DB_PASSWORD" or "file:/etc/orkstack/secrets/db". Orker policy decides which schemes exist. |

### SetCurrentOrkflowVersionRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `version` | `string` | must already exist |
| `namespace` | `string` | empty = the default namespace |
| `acknowledge_breaking` | `bool` | acknowledge_breaking permits a promotion whose target BREAKS the declared interface of the version runs execute now. Without it such a promotion is FailedPrecondition and nothing moves. It permits; it never requires: set on a compatible promotion it changes nothing. It accepts the break against whichever version the pointer names when the request is served. |

### SetCurrentOrkflowVersionResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` |  |
| `namespace` | `string` |  |
| `current_version` | `string` |  |
| `previous_version` | `string` | previous_version is what the pointer named before, empty when it was never set. It is what a rollback promotes back to. |
| `updated_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `interface_verdict` | [`InterfaceVerdict`](#interfaceverdict) | interface_verdict is the promoted version's declared interface compared with compared_version — what ran when no version was named, until now. UNSPECIFIED, with compared_version empty, when the promotion did not change what runs. BREAKING here means the request acknowledged it. |
| `compared_version` | `string` |  |

### StreamEventsRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `string` |  |
| `from_sequence` | `int64` |  |
| `namespace` | `string` | empty = the default namespace |

### StreamTaskLogsRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `string` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `attempt` | `int32` | attempt selects one try of the task. 0 means the latest attempt that has written anything, so a caller that never saw a retry does not have to know retries exist.<br><br>With `follow`, 0 keeps meaning THE LATEST for as long as the stream is open, not merely when it opened. A retry is invisible in a task's status — the task stays RUNNING while try 2 starts under a new key prefix — so a stream that resolved the attempt once would sit on a dead attempt, delivering nothing, for the rest of the task's life, and say it was live. When a later attempt appears the stream moves to it and delivers that attempt from its FIRST chunk; every chunk names the attempt it belongs to, and its seq restarts at 1, so a client can tell a new attempt from more of the old one. A non-zero attempt is pinned and never moves. |
| `from_seq` | `int64` | from_seq resumes AFTER this sequence: it is the LAST chunk sequence the client already received, and the stream continues with the next one. 0 starts at the beginning. It is the same contract StreamEvents.from_sequence has, over the log's own numbering — dense and 1-based per (run, task, attempt) — so a client that hands back the seq of the last chunk it saw replays nothing twice and misses nothing, even when it reconnects to a DIFFERENT replica. |
| `from_attempt` | `int32` | from_attempt says which attempt from_seq counts chunks of. It is what makes a resume safe across a retry: seq is dense per ATTEMPT, so a cursor of 500 handed back after try 1 would silently skip try 2's first 500 chunks — or, since try 2 is usually shorter, would deliver nothing at all while the pane read LIVE.<br><br>0 means "the attempt this request resolves to", which is what a first connection means and what a client pinning `attempt` means. When it names a DIFFERENT attempt from the one resolved, from_seq is dropped and the resolved attempt is delivered from its first chunk: a new attempt is a new read, not a continuation of the old one. |
| `follow` | `bool` | follow keeps the stream open for chunks that do not exist yet, ending when the task reaches a terminal state. False makes it a replay: the chunks the store holds when the request is served, then the end — whether or not the task is still writing, so a replay never turns into a follow. |
| `namespace` | `string` | empty = the default namespace |
| `item` | optional `int32` | item names the item of a fan-out task_id whose output is streamed; required for a fan-out task, refused for any other. attempt, from_seq and from_attempt then count that item's own attempts and chunks. |

### SubmitRunRequest

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` | orkflow name |
| `orkflow_version` | `string` | orkflow version; empty = latest |
| `input` | [`Payload`](#payload) |  |
| `idempotency_key` | `string` | optional dedupe |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace selects which namespace's orkflow_name is submitted. Empty is the default namespace. A name is unique WITHIN a namespace, so this is half of the orkflow's address, not a filter. |
| `allow_empty_pool` | `bool` | allow_empty_pool submits even when a task's resolved pool has no live Orkers. Default false: an empty pool is an error at submit, not a run that reaches RUNNING and stays there because nothing will ever pick its tasks up. Setting it is logged with the pool it overrode. |
| `origin_reference` | `string` | origin_reference is caller-supplied correlation text recorded as RunOrigin.reference: a CI job URL, a ticket key, an event id. Optional. At most 256 bytes and no control characters (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise, before a run id is minted). Opaque to OrkStack. On the trigger door the same value arrives as the Ork-Origin-Reference header, so a CI job sets one header and the body stays exactly the run's input. |
| `source_run_id` | `string` | source_run_id marks this submission as a re-run of an existing run: origin.kind becomes RUN_AGAIN and origin.id this value. Set by `orkctl run again` and the run page's Run again. The server confirms the run exists IN THIS NAMESPACE before minting anything; an unknown id, or a run of another namespace, is NOT_FOUND naming it, on the rule every run read follows. It is never an idempotency key and never reuses one: a re-run is a new execution with a new id (docs/UI_CLI_PARITY.md). |
| `no_cache` | `bool` | no_cache runs this submission without reading any memo: every cached task runs its container and refreshes its memo. It applies to every run the submission starts, child runs included. It does nothing for an Orkflow that declares no cache:. |

### SubmitRunResponse

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `run` | [`Run`](#run) |  |
| `await_callbacks` | repeated [`AwaitCallback`](#awaitcallback) | await_callbacks holds one entry per await of the definition that declares `callback: true`, in declaration order. It is populated ONLY by the call that started the run: a keyed repeat that returned an existing run, and every read, carry none — the plaintext no longer exists anywhere. |

### Task

Task is a single node in the orkflow DAG. It maps to exactly one activity
execution on an Orker, and an activity is an OCI image.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | unique within the orkflow |
| `with` | `google.protobuf.Struct` | with holds the activity-specific configuration (templated). |
| `needs` | repeated `string` | needs lists task ids that must complete before this task runs (DAG edges). |
| `condition` | `string` | condition is a Go template rendered by the engine; the task is skipped when it renders one of the documented falsy spellings (docs/DSL.md "Templating"). |
| `timeout_seconds` | `int32` | default 300 |
| `retry` | [`RetryPolicy`](#retrypolicy) |  |
| `pool` | `string` | pool names the set of Orkers this task runs on. Empty means the deployment's default pool, which answers to the name "main"; Namespace.default_pool joins that resolution.<br><br>Writing "main" and writing nothing are ONE route, always: "main" is a name for the deployment's default pool and not for one fixed set of Orkers, so wherever an operator has pointed the default, both spellings go there and both are reported on the pool that answers for it. Within a run, one pool name means one set of Orkers, in both directions. The engine maps a pool to its internal route and nowhere else. |
| `uses` | `string` | uses is what the author wrote: a catalog activity name ("shell") or a registry reference ("ghcr.io/acme/migrate:v3", "repo@sha256:..."). It is the only image-selecting field in the DSL. |
| `image` | [`ImageRef`](#imageref) | image is the engine's apply-time resolution of uses. It is stamped into the immutable version document, so re-applying the same YAML after a tag moves produces a different definition (§4.4). |
| `command` | repeated `string` |  |
| `env` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; |  |
| `secrets` | repeated [`SecretRef`](#secretref) |  |
| `resources` | [`ResourceRequest`](#resourcerequest) |  |
| `network` | [`NetworkMode`](#networkmode) |  |
| `cancellation_grace_period_seconds` | `int32` |  |
| `run_as_orker_user` | `bool` | run_as_orker_user is the §3.1 escape hatch, per task. It changes what runs, so it is part of canonicalOrkflow(Task) (§4.4). |
| `pin` | `string` | pin names the Pin this task belongs to, or is empty. Every task of one pin runs on one Orker process and sees the same /orkstack/shared. It changes what runs and where, so it is part of canonicalOrkflow(Task) — emitted ONLY when set, so a definition with no pin keeps its digest. |
| `await` | [`AwaitSpec`](#awaitspec) | await makes this an awaited task. Mutually exclusive with uses and with every field that shapes a container (docs/DSL.md rules 6 and 15): an awaited task has no image, no pool, and no timeout_seconds of its own. |
| `each` | [`EachSpec`](#eachspec) | each makes this task a fan-out. A fan-out has uses:, like any container task; it may not name a pin (docs/DSL.md rule 23) and an awaited task may not carry it (rule 15). |
| `orkflow` | [`OrkflowRef`](#orkflowref) | orkflow is the apply-time resolution of `uses: orkflow:<name>@<version>`, the analogue of image for a container task. A composed task starts a CHILD RUN of exactly that definition, in this Orkflow's namespace, and reaches no Orker: it carries no image, pool, pin, retry, timeout or other execution field (docs/DSL.md rules 26–27). Part of canonicalOrkflow(Task) only when set (see pin), so this Orkflow's digest pins the child's. |
| `cache` | [`CacheSpec`](#cachespec) | cache opts this container task into memoization across runs. It may not name a pin (docs/DSL.md rule 36), and an awaited or composed task may not carry it (rules 15, 27). |
| `join` | [`JoinPolicy`](#joinpolicy) | join is when this task may start, decided from how its needs ended (docs/DSL.md "Joins and failure handlers"). UNSPECIFIED is all_succeeded. Part of canonicalOrkflow(Task) ONLY when set (see pin), so a definition with no join keeps its digest. A task whose join is ANY_FAILED or ALL_DONE is a failure handler: it may not name a pin, carry each or carry cache (docs/DSL.md rule 39). |

### TaskAttempt

TaskAttempt is the immutable record of ONE Temporal attempt of one task,
written by the Orker that ran it at the end of the attempt (§7.1). It is the
failure-side sibling of ActivityCommit: a commit says what the winning
attempt produced, an attempt record says what EVERY attempt did, including
the ones that lost.

Temporal owns retries, so the workflow only ever sees a task's final
outcome — an intermediate attempt's error reaches nothing that outlives the
Orker process. This record is what makes it durable, and it is written
best-effort: a record that cannot be stored is logged, never allowed to
change what the attempt itself reported.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `int32` | schema_version is 1. A reader that does not know the value ignores the record rather than guessing, exactly as ActivityCommit's does. |
| `run_id` | `string` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `attempt` | `int32` | attempt is activity.GetInfo(ctx).Attempt, 1-based. |
| `outcome` | [`AttemptOutcome`](#attemptoutcome) |  |
| `error` | [`Error`](#error) | error is set only for FAILED, and carries the same shape TaskRun.error does: the §8.2 reason as code, the category, retryability, the Orker's message, and its scan notes as details. |
| `exit_code` | `int32` | exit_code is the container's exit status, 0 when the container never ran. |
| `started_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `finished_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `orker_id` | `string` | orker_id is the Orker that executed this attempt. "Which Orker failed" is the retry question, so the record answers it without a log search. |
| `pool` | `string` | pool is the routing request this attempt was dispatched with, as TaskRun.pool spells it. |
| `phase` | `string` | phase is the §7.1 phase the attempt ended in — "image", "run", "commit", … — the same name as the last element of phases below. |
| `image` | [`ImageRef`](#imageref) | image is the ImageRef as executed, with platform_digest and delivery set. |
| `system_artifacts` | repeated [`ArtifactRef`](#artifactref) | system_artifacts are the stdout.log/stderr.log references, when this attempt got as far as uploading them. |
| `commit_adopted` | `bool` | commit_adopted is true when this attempt found an existing commit and returned it without running the container (§5.4). |
| `build_id` | `string` | build_id is ORK_BUILD_ID of the Orker that ran the attempt. |
| `phases` | repeated [`PhaseSpan`](#phasespan) | phases lists every §7.1 phase this attempt passed through, in order, contiguous, the last ending at finished_at, and its last element's phase equal to `phase` above. Empty on a record written before this field existed and on a synthesized UNREPORTED row. A reader renders an empty list as unavailable, never as "no phases happened".<br><br>schema_version stays 1: the field is additive and UnmarshalAttempt discards unknown fields, so a record with phases reads on a build without them and a record without phases reads on this one as an empty list. |
| `resources` | [`ReservedResources`](#reservedresources) | resources is what this Orker reserved for the attempt. Set on every record whose request the Orker's policy admitted — including an attempt that adopted a commit or failed before its container started, because the Orker's slot was committed to it either way. Unset when the request was refused (RESOURCE_REQUEST_REFUSED), on a record written before this field existed, and on a synthesized UNREPORTED row. A reader never treats unset as zero: usage counts such an attempt's held time and reports it as carrying no reservation. schema_version stays 1: the field is additive and UnmarshalAttempt discards unknown fields. |
| `item` | optional `int32` | item is set when this attempt ran one item of a fan-out task: that item's 0-based index. The record then lives under the item's own key (metadata/attempts/{run}/{task}/{item}/{attempt}.json). schema_version stays 1: the field is additive and UnmarshalAttempt discards unknown fields. |
| `cache` | [`CacheResult`](#cacheresult) | cache is this attempt's memo decision, key_components included. Set only for an attempt of a cached task that reached the memo step; a HIT records outcome SUCCEEDED, phase "memo", exit_code 0, no system_artifacts (it uploaded none) and image equal to the input's pinned ImageRef with no platform (it pulled nothing). |

### TaskAwait

TaskAwait is an awaited task's own state on the run snapshot. It is SET for
every task whose definition declares `await:` — from the run's first
snapshot, while the task is still PENDING — and UNSET for every other
task, so a snapshot of a run with no await is byte-identical to what it was
before this message existed. Its presence is how a client tells an awaited
task from a container task without reading the definition.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `callback` | `bool` | callback mirrors AwaitSpec.callback: whether a callback token was minted. |
| `deadline` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | deadline is when the await times out, on the workflow's clock. Unset until the task starts awaiting. |
| `resolved_via` | [`AwaitResolvedVia`](#awaitresolvedvia) | resolved_via and resolved_by are set when a resolution was APPLIED — completed or rejected — and never for a timeout or a cancellation. |
| `resolved_by` | `string` | resolved_by is the Ork-Principal assertion on the resolving request, bounded to 256 bytes: recorded as asserted and NEVER authenticated, the word control-plane-audit-trail and run-origin use. Empty when none was sent. |

### TaskChild

TaskChild is a composed task's own state on the run snapshot. It is SET for
every task whose definition declares `uses: orkflow:` — from the run's first
snapshot, while the task is still PENDING — and UNSET for every other task,
so a snapshot of a run with no composed task is byte-identical to what it
was before this message existed.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` | The child Orkflow as the parent pinned it (Task.orkflow). |
| `orkflow_version` | `string` |  |
| `orkflow_definition_digest` | `string` |  |
| `run_id` | `string` | run_id is the child run, set once its start is CONFIRMED and never before: an id whose start was refused names no run. The child run's own Run.origin is {PARENT_RUN, &lt;this run's id>}. |

### TaskEach

TaskEach is a fan-out task's own state on the run snapshot. It is SET for
every task whose definition declares `each:` — from the run's first
snapshot, while the task is still PENDING — and UNSET for every other task,
so a snapshot of a run with no fan-out is byte-identical to what it was
before this message existed.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `expanded` | `bool` | expanded is true once the array was counted and the items created. It stays false while PENDING, when the task was SKIPPED, and when the array could not be counted (the task then FAILED with an EACH_* code). |
| `count` | `int32` | count is the number of items, equal to len(TaskRun.items), once expanded. |

### TaskLogChunk

TaskLogChunk is one slice of a task attempt's output, exactly as the Orker
flushed it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | `string` |  |
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `attempt` | `int32` |  |
| `seq` | `int64` | seq orders the chunk within (run_id, task_id, attempt): dense, starting at 1. It is assigned by the single Orker executing the attempt, so it is total and gap-free without any coordination, and it is what a client hands back as from_seq. |
| `data` | `bytes` | data is UTF-8 log bytes ending on a line boundary, except where one line exceeded the chunk limit and was split. |
| `truncated` | `bool` | truncated marks the notice chunk the Orker writes when a task's output passed its cap. Its data says so in words; no further output was stored. Truncation is visible in the stream, never silent. |
| `last` | `bool` | last marks the end of the stream: everything this stream will deliver has been delivered, and its seq is the last sequence sent, so a client resumes from it. With follow that means the task reached a terminal state; without follow it means the replay is complete. It carries no data. |
| `item` | optional `int32` | item echoes the request's item. |

### TaskRun

TaskRun is the execution record of a single Task within a Run.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `task_id` | `string` |  |
| `status` | [`Status`](#status) |  |
| `attempt` | `int32` |  |
| `output` | [`Payload`](#payload) | output carries the inline values.json when one was inlined, decoded for display only. values_ref is the authoritative reference. |
| `artifacts` | repeated [`ArtifactRef`](#artifactref) |  |
| `error` | [`Error`](#error) | carries FailureCategory (§8) |
| `started_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | started_at is when the Orker began the attempt that produced this task's outcome, on the Orker's own clock: ExecuteTaskResult.started_at for a succeeded task (the committing attempt's start for an adopted commit, exactly as `attempt` is the committing attempt), and ActivityFailureDetail.started_at for a failed one. It is the start of the FINAL attempt, on the same rule attempt, error, exit_code and orker_id already follow: the snapshot describes the attempt that decided the task, and ListTaskAttempts describes the rest.<br><br>Unset while the task is PENDING or RUNNING, and for a terminal task no Orker reported on — a host that died before reporting, a Temporal-side timeout, a cancellation that reached the Orker as a plain context cancellation, a lost pin. Unset is "not known", never zero.<br><br>Before this field's meaning was corrected it held the dispatch instant; scheduled_at (18) holds that now.<br><br>For an awaited task, both are the instant the task started awaiting, on the workflow's clock: it is never queued and no Orker reports on it. |
| `finished_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | finished_at is the workflow's own clock at the moment it learned this task's outcome. |
| `pool` | `string` | pool names the set of Orkers this attempt was dispatched to, in the word its author typed: the task's own `pool:`, or the pool this run's default route resolves to when the task named none.<br><br>Within a run, one pool name means one set of Orkers, so naming this pool on a task reaches exactly the Orkers this attempt reached. That holds under the per-deployment route override operators use to keep two stacks apart: a route belonging to no pool reports as the built-in "main", and a task that writes "main" follows the same override instead of escaping it. The override is an operator concern this contract does not expose, so this name is the routing request rather than a measurement of the host that answered, and another deployment resolves it against its own Orkers.<br><br>Empty means the task never reached an Orker (skipped, or terminal before dispatch). |
| `values_ref` | [`ArtifactRef`](#artifactref) | values_ref addresses the committed values.json for this attempt. Set whenever the task succeeded, whether or not output was inlined. |
| `commit` | [`CommitRef`](#commitref) | commit references the durable completion record (§5). |
| `exit_code` | `int32` | exit_code is the container's exit status as reported by the Orker. |
| `system_artifacts` | repeated [`ArtifactRef`](#artifactref) | system_artifacts are stdout.log and stderr.log for this attempt. |
| `retry_state` | [`RetryState`](#retrystate) | retry_state says why Temporal stopped retrying this task, read off temporal.ActivityError.RetryState() when the task ended in an error. It is DERIVED data on the snapshot — the engine records what Temporal already decided, it does not decide anything with it.<br><br>Unset for SUCCEEDED and SKIPPED tasks, for a failure that never reached an activity, and for snapshots written before this field existed. |
| `pin` | `string` | pin is the Pin this task belongs to, as the author named it, or empty. Two TaskRuns of one run with the same pin ran on the same Orker. |
| `orker_id` | `string` | orker_id is the Orker that produced this task's final outcome, read off ExecuteTaskResult.orker_id or ActivityFailureDetail.orker_id. Set for every task that reached an Orker, pinned or not; empty when the task never reached one (skipped, canceled before dispatch) or when the Orker died before reporting (heartbeat timeout).<br><br>One exception to "reported by this task's own attempt": a task recorded PIN_HOST_LOST or PIN_TIMEOUT reports nothing at all — its host died — so the engine BACKFILLS this from another member of the same pin. A pin never moves: every member executes on the same Orker process for the pin's whole life, so a sibling's orker_id is this task's by construction. It stays empty only when no member of that pin ever reported one, in which case the failure's error.details carries the pin host's raw OS host name as an explicitly labelled best-effort lead, which is NOT an orker_id. Empty on a fan-out task's own row, whose items each carry their own. |
| `scheduled_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | scheduled_at is the instant the engine scheduled this task's activity — workflow.Now at schedule(), which is also the timestamp on the EVENT_TYPE_TASK_SCHEDULED event. It is a PROJECTION of that event onto the snapshot, not a new measurement, and it is the workflow's own deterministic clock, never an Orker's.<br><br>Unset when the task never reached scheduling (skipped, or canceled before dispatch) and on a snapshot written before this field existed. The two are told apart by started_at: a pre-contract snapshot has started_at set (it held the dispatch instant then) and scheduled_at unset; a never-scheduled task has neither.<br><br>For an awaited task, both are the instant the task started awaiting, on the workflow's clock: it is never queued and no Orker reports on it. |
| `await` | [`TaskAwait`](#taskawait) | await is this task's await state, set for a task whose definition declares `await:` and unset otherwise (see TaskAwait). |
| `each` | [`TaskEach`](#taskeach) | each is set for a fan-out task's own row (TaskEach). |
| `items` | repeated [`TaskRun`](#taskrun) | items are a fan-out's items, one per element of the expanded array, in index order; empty until expansion and for every task that is not a fan-out. Each element is a TaskRun whose task_id is this task's id and whose `item` is set; the fields below mean for an item what they mean for a task (its own attempt, commit, values_ref, artifacts, logs, orker, error, times). An item never carries `output` (its values are read through values_ref), `each`, `items`, `pin` or `await`.<br><br>This row itself is the AGGREGATE: its status is the fan-out's, its error is the error of the item that failed it (message prefixed "item N of M failed:"), its scheduled_at is the expansion instant, its started_at the earliest item's, and its attempt, exit_code, orker_id, commit, values_ref, artifacts and system_artifacts are unset — those belong to items.<br><br>ListRuns never carries items (only GetRun does), and neither does a webhook body or the workflow's own result. |
| `item` | optional `int32` | item is set on an element of `items`: its 0-based index. Unset on every row of Run.task_runs. |
| `child` | [`TaskChild`](#taskchild) | child is set for a composed task (TaskChild). Such a task reaches no Orker: pool, pin, orker_id, attempt, exit_code, commit, artifacts and system_artifacts stay unset, and values_ref addresses the child's declared outputs as stored for THIS run. |
| `cache` | [`CacheResult`](#cacheresult) | cache is the memo decision of the attempt that produced this task's outcome (CacheResult, key_components never set here). Set only for a cached task that SUCCEEDED on an Orker that implements caching; unset for every other row — so a snapshot of a run with no cached task is byte-identical — and for a cached task that failed, whose attempts carry what each memo step decided. On a fan-out it is set on the items, never on the fan-out's own row. |
| `join` | [`JoinPolicy`](#joinpolicy) | join is the task's join policy, set from the run's first snapshot for every task whose definition declares one other than all_succeeded, and UNSET otherwise — so a snapshot of a run with no join is byte-identical to what it was before this field existed. Its presence is how a client tells a failure handler from an ordinary task without reading the definition (the precedent of TaskRun.await, .each and .child). |

### TelemetryPolicy

TelemetryPolicy is a namespace's selection among the deployment's
telemetry sinks (AGENTS.md §6): a namespace admin chooses WHERE among the
operator's declared destinations, not the destination itself. It can never
name an endpoint or a credential.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sink` | `string` | sink is a name in the deployment's sink table (ORK_TELEMETRY_SINKS); empty means "default". Validated at write time against the engine's table, so a stored name is one the deployment knew — the same rule default_pool follows against the pool table. |
| `task_logs` | [`TaskLogExport`](#tasklogexport) | task_logs overrides the Orker's ORK_ORKER_TASK_LOG_EXPORT for this namespace's runs. UNSPECIFIED inherits it; ENABLED and DISABLED override it either way. |
| `attributes` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; | attributes are exported on every signal of this namespace's runs as ork.ns.&lt;key>. Bounded: at most 16 entries, key ^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$, value at most 256 bytes, and a key under ork., service., or host. is refused because those namespaces are the platform's own. |

### TelemetrySelection

TelemetrySelection is what an Orker needs to route one task's signals: the
sink by name, the task-log switch, and the attributes to stamp. Decided at
SUBMIT from the namespace's TelemetryPolicy and the orkflow's labels
(engine.RunPlan.Telemetry), and carried on both ExecuteTaskInput and Run so
the decision replays identically and is visible on the run record. Never
an endpoint, never a credential.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sink` | `string` |  |
| `task_logs` | [`TaskLogExport`](#tasklogexport) |  |
| `attributes` | map&lt;`string`, `string`&gt; |  |

### UpdateScheduleRequest

UpdateScheduleRequest replaces every mutable field with the value here: an
unset input clears the input, an unset description clears it. A client
that wants to change one thing reads the schedule and sends the rest back,
which is what `orkctl schedule update` does.

There is deliberately no etag. The Go SDK issues a schedule update without
a conflict token (v1.47.0, internal/internal_schedule_client.go:303), so a
compare-and-swap here would be a promise the mechanism underneath cannot
keep. Last writer wins, and this comment says so rather than a field
implying otherwise.

### UsageRow

UsageRow is one group's reserved consumption, or the namespace total.

A key dimension NOT in the response's group_by is empty and means "not
grouped by". The total row has every key empty.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orkflow_name` | `string` | Run.orkflow_name |
| `task_id` | `string` | TaskRun.task_id |
| `pool` | `string` | TaskRun.pool — where the task was dispatched |
| `runs` | `int64` | runs is how many distinct finished runs dispatched at least one task into this row. |
| `tasks` | `int64` | tasks is how many dispatched tasks (TaskRun.pool set) are in this row, with or without an attempt record. |
| `attempts` | `int64` | attempts is how many attempt RECORDS were read for this row. Attempts that left none are unreported_attempts, never counted here. |
| `task_seconds` | `double` | task_seconds is the sum of held time (finished_at − started_at) over the row's recorded attempts that have both instants in order. |
| `cpu_seconds` | `double` | cpu_seconds and gib_seconds are reservation × held time over the row's recorded attempts that carry a reservation. RESERVED, not used. |
| `gib_seconds` | `double` |  |
| `attempts_without_resources` | `int64` | attempts_without_resources counts recorded attempts with a usable interval and no reservation — written before TaskAttempt.resources existed, by an Orker of an older release, or refused before a reservation was resolved. Their held time IS in task_seconds; they add nothing to cpu_seconds or gib_seconds, which are lower bounds whenever this is nonzero. |
| `attempts_unmeasured` | `int64` | attempts_unmeasured counts recorded attempts missing started_at or finished_at, or finishing before they started. They contribute to no sum. No Orker of this tree writes one; the count exists so a record from another writer is visible instead of silently zero. |
| `unreported_attempts` | `int64` | unreported_attempts counts attempts numbered below a task's highest that have no record — the Orker running them died or lost its heartbeat before filing one. Their consumption is unknown and not counted. |

### Webhook

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `url` | `string` |  |
| `events` | repeated [`EventType`](#eventtype) | events selects the transitions this subscription wants. Empty means every RUN transition — and only those: a task outcome event (TASK_SCHEDULED, TASK_STARTED, TASK_SUCCEEDED, TASK_FAILED) is delivered only to a subscription that names it. TASK_LOG is never accepted. |
| `created_at` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` |  |
| `namespace` | `string` | namespace narrows this subscription to runs of one namespace. Empty means every namespace, which is what every subscription registered before this field existed is. A run that names no namespace is in "default", so a subscription written as "default" matches it. |
| `orkflow_name` | `string` | orkflow_name narrows to runs of one orkflow, by the name the author wrote. Empty means every orkflow. It composes with namespace by conjunction and does not require it: a name alone matches that name in every namespace. |
| `task_id` | `string` | task_id narrows the task outcome events to one task. Empty means every task. It is consulted only for TASK_* events: a RUN_* event has no task and passes this filter unconditionally, so one subscription can want TASK_SUCCEEDED of `extract` and RUN_FAILED of the whole run. Registration refuses a task_id when events names no TASK_* event, because the filter could then never be consulted. |
| `name` | `string` | name is the operator's handle: a slug, at most 200 bytes, unique among the named subscriptions of its namespace scope. It REQUIRES namespace: a name is unique within one namespace, and a deployment-wide subscription belongs to none. Empty means unnamed — every subscription registered before this field existed — and an unnamed subscription is outside every automation document. It plays no part in delivery. |

| `ATTEMPT_OUTCOME_UNREPORTED` | 4 | UNREPORTED is never written by an Orker. A reader synthesizes it for an attempt number that has no record, which means the Orker running it died or lost its heartbeat before it could write one. |

### FilterOperator

FilterOperator is the CLOSED set of comparisons a list filter may make.
Every filter of a request must hold (AND). There is no OR, no negation of
a group, no nesting and no expression, and there never will be one here
(AGENTS.md §13). docs/UI_CLI_PARITY.md "Filtering lists" is the contract;
the CLI spelling of each operator is in the trailing comment.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | refused |
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_EQUALS` | 1 | exactly one value f=v |
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_NOT_EQUALS` | 2 | exactly one value f!=v |
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_IN` | 3 | 1 to 64 values, any matches f=v1,v2 |
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_CONTAINS` | 4 | one non-empty value; text f~v |
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_PREFIX` | 5 | one non-empty value; text f^v |
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_AT_OR_AFTER` | 6 | one instant, inclusive f>=t |
| `FILTER_OPERATOR_BEFORE` | 7 | one instant, exclusive f&lt;t |

| `HEARTBEAT_UNAVAILABLE_REASON_NOT_STARTED` | 1 | NOT_STARTED: state is SCHEDULED (or UNSPECIFIED); no Orker has the attempt, so there is nothing to beat. |
| `HEARTBEAT_UNAVAILABLE_REASON_NO_HEARTBEAT_YET` | 2 | NO_HEARTBEAT_YET: an Orker has the attempt and no beat from THIS attempt has arrived — including the case where the cluster still holds a previous attempt's detail. On a healthy Orker this lasts one tick at most, because the loop beats immediately on start. |
| `HEARTBEAT_UNAVAILABLE_REASON_UNDECODABLE` | 3 | UNDECODABLE: a beat from this attempt arrived whose detail is not the Orker's shape (no "phase"). Reported, never guessed at. |

InterfaceVerdict is how one version's DECLARED interface — its inputs:
and its outputs: — compares with another's.

| Value | Number | Description |

### JoinPolicy

JoinPolicy is when a task with needs may start, decided from how its needs
ended (docs/DSL.md "Joins and failure handlers"). Defined here rather than
in orkflow.proto for the reason CacheScope is: activity.proto cannot import
orkflow.proto, and JoinContext below carries it.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `JOIN_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | UNSPECIFIED is all_succeeded: the task starts when every need SUCCEEDED, and a SKIPPED need skips it. It is the ONLY encoding of the default — the compiler writes it for `join: all_succeeded` and for no `join:` — so a definition that names no join keeps its digest and every payload stays byte-identical. |
| `JOIN_POLICY_NONE_FAILED` | 1 | NONE_FAILED: every need terminal, none FAILED or CANCELED, at least one SUCCEEDED. SKIPPED needs are tolerated, which is what lets branches re-join. |
| `JOIN_POLICY_ANY_FAILED` | 2 | ANY_FAILED: at least one need FAILED, after its retries. A failure handler: one of the two kinds of task that start in a failing run. |
| `JOIN_POLICY_ALL_DONE` | 3 | ALL_DONE: every need terminal, whatever its outcome. A failure handler. |

### LiveAttemptState

LiveAttemptState is where the pending attempt is in Temporal's view. It
mirrors temporal.api.enums.v1.PendingActivityState with its own numbering,
on the rule RetryState (run.proto) follows: a value of another package's
enum is never carried by number, and the mapping is an explicit switch in
internal/engine/live.go. PAUSED and PAUSE_REQUESTED have no member: nothing
in OrkStack pauses an activity, and a reader of an older build must not be
handed a state it cannot name — they map to UNSPECIFIED.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LIVE_ATTEMPT_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `LIVE_ATTEMPT_STATE_SCHEDULED` | 1 | SCHEDULED: Temporal holds the activity and no Orker has it — the pool has no free Orker, or a retry is waiting out its backoff (next_attempt_at is then set). |
| `LIVE_ATTEMPT_STATE_STARTED` | 2 | STARTED: an Orker picked the attempt up. Only STARTED and CANCEL_REQUESTED can carry a heartbeat. |
| `LIVE_ATTEMPT_STATE_CANCEL_REQUESTED` | 3 | CANCEL_REQUESTED: the run was cancelled and the Orker has been (or is about to be) told through a heartbeat response; the §3.3 SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL sequence runs on the Orker while this state holds. |

### NetworkMode

NetworkMode is the complete set of network configurations an Orkflow may
select. Named Orker-defined profiles are deliberately absent (AGENTS.md §6).

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NETWORK_MODE_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | treated as NETWORK_MODE_DEFAULT |
| `NETWORK_MODE_DEFAULT` | 1 |  |
| `NETWORK_MODE_NONE` | 2 |  |

### OrkflowCallerKind

OrkflowCallerKind is what references an orkflow.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ORKFLOW_CALLER_KIND_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `ORKFLOW_CALLER_KIND_ORKFLOW` | 1 | ORKFLOW: a composed task (uses: orkflow:&lt;name>@&lt;version>) of a stored version of another orkflow. It always pins a version and is never moved by a promotion. |
| `ORKFLOW_CALLER_KIND_TRIGGER` | 2 |  |
| `ORKFLOW_CALLER_KIND_SCHEDULE` | 3 |  |

### OverlapPolicy

OverlapPolicy is what happens when a fire is due while the run of an
earlier fire is still executing. Each value is the Temporal
ScheduleOverlapPolicy of the same name, applied to the RUN: the fire
workflow lives exactly as long as the run it started, so "still running"
means the run is still running. TERMINATE_OTHER is deliberately absent:
termination bypasses workflow code, and a terminated fire would leave its
run executing while claiming otherwise.

Every declared number equals the number of the same-named Temporal value
(go.temporal.io/api/enums/v1 ScheduleOverlapPolicy, v1.63.4), and 5 —
Temporal's TERMINATE_OTHER — is RESERVED, so ALLOW_ALL is 6 here as it is
there. The alignment is for readability only. The engine converts through
an explicit switch that never casts (specOverlapToTemporal /
overrideOverlapToTemporal), and an undeclared value such as 5
arriving on the wire (proto3 enums are open) is refused by the API and by
that switch; it never reaches the cluster.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OVERLAP_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | UNSPECIFIED has TWO meanings, fixed by the field that carries it: on ScheduleSpec.overlap (create, update) it is recorded as SKIP, the cluster's own default, so no read ever returns UNSPECIFIED; on FireScheduleRequest.overlap and BackfillScheduleRequest.overlap it is "no override" and the schedule's own policy applies. |
| `OVERLAP_POLICY_SKIP` | 1 | SKIP: the due fire is dropped. Counted in fires_skipped_overlap. |
| `OVERLAP_POLICY_BUFFER_ONE` | 2 | BUFFER_ONE: at most one due fire waits and starts when the run ends. |
| `OVERLAP_POLICY_BUFFER_ALL` | 3 | BUFFER_ALL: every due fire waits and they start one after another. |
| `OVERLAP_POLICY_CANCEL_OTHER` | 4 | CANCEL_OTHER: the earlier run is cancelled — SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL, exactly as `run cancel` — and the due fire starts without waiting for it to finish; the two overlap for the cancelled run's grace period. |
| `OVERLAP_POLICY_ALLOW_ALL` | 6 | ALLOW_ALL: fires never wait for one another. 6, not 5: see above. |

### PlanOutcome

PlanOutcome is what the interpreter would do with one task, given the
planned input and the request's assumed failures. It is deliberately not
orkstack.v1.Status: a plan executes nothing, and the enum must not be
mistaken for an execution record. FAILS is a decision the interpreter would
itself take (a condition it cannot evaluate); ASSUMED_FAILED is the
request's assumption, never a prediction that the task fails.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PLAN_OUTCOME_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `PLAN_OUTCOME_RUNS` | 1 | RUNS: the interpreter would schedule this task's activity. |
| `PLAN_OUTCOME_SKIPPED` | 2 | SKIPPED: the interpreter would mark it STATUS_SKIPPED, for the reason in PlanTask.skip_reason, without reaching an Orker. |
| `PLAN_OUTCOME_FAILS` | 3 | FAILS: evaluating this task's condition returns an error. Unless an earlier task already did, the run starts failing at that point (RUN_FAILED with the error's text); in a definition with a failure handler the interpreter also records the task FAILED (CONDITION_FAILED). A FAILS of a failure handler decided after fails_at is recorded on that handler and cuts nothing, so a plan of a definition with failure handlers may hold more than one FAILS; without a failure handler it holds at most one. PlanTask.error carries it. |
| `PLAN_OUTCOME_UNREACHED` | 4 | UNREACHED: a task that is not a failure handler and is certainly never started: it transitively needs an ASSUMED_FAILED task, or a FAILS of a task that is not a failure handler was decided before it (unreached_by names which); only present when fails_at is set. |
| `PLAN_OUTCOME_AWAITS` | 5 | AWAITS: the task is an awaited task the interpreter would open: it takes a wave as RUNS does and starts no activity. |
| `PLAN_OUTCOME_ASSUMED_FAILED` | 6 | ASSUMED_FAILED: the request's assume_failed names this task and it would run; it is planned as having run and FAILED. It takes a wave as RUNS does, contributes no output, and is where the planned run starts failing unless an earlier task already did. |

### ReferenceState

ReferenceState is the addressed run's OWN standing in the object index.
It exists so an empty `references` list can be read: "released" and
"never recorded" are different facts that would otherwise render alike.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `REFERENCE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `REFERENCE_STATE_HELD` | 1 | HELD: the run is archived and its marker on this object is present. |
| `REFERENCE_STATE_RELEASED` | 2 | RELEASED: no marker, and the run's cleanup record exists — the cleanup worker released its object claims (docs/STORAGE.md, "Reclaiming space"). released_at carries the record's timestamp. |
| `REFERENCE_STATE_ABSENT` | 3 | ABSENT: no marker and no cleanup record. The run has not reached its terminal event, its archive write has not completed, it was archived before the object index existed, or cleanup released its markers and had not yet written its record. The server does not guess which; a client renders "no reference recorded", never "released" and never "held". |

### ReleaseBlockerKind

ReleaseBlockerKind names why a release may not take new runs right now.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RELEASE_BLOCKER_KIND_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `RELEASE_BLOCKER_KIND_NO_ENGINE` | 1 | NO_ENGINE: no engine process of the release is running, so a run sent to it would never start. |
| `RELEASE_BLOCKER_KIND_POOL_NOT_SERVED` | 2 | POOL_NOT_SERVED: `pool` is in use and no uncordoned Orker of the release serves it. |
| `RELEASE_BLOCKER_KIND_PINS_NOT_HOSTED` | 3 | PINS_NOT_HOSTED: `pool` has a pin host of another release and no uncordoned Orker of this release in it hosts pins. |
| `RELEASE_BLOCKER_KIND_UNVERSIONED_RUNS` | 4 | UNVERSIONED_RUNS: no release is current yet and runs started before any was are still executing; making this release take new runs would move them onto it mid-run. |
| `RELEASE_BLOCKER_KIND_UNVERIFIED` | 5 | UNVERIFIED: part of the evidence could not be read, so the release cannot be shown to pass. Never treated as passing. |

### ReleaseDrainState

ReleaseDrainState is the cluster's own verdict on a PREVIOUS release.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RELEASE_DRAIN_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | UNSPECIFIED: not applicable — the release is current, ramping, or a candidate, and the cluster keeps no drain state for it. |
| `RELEASE_DRAIN_STATE_DRAINING` | 1 | DRAINING: runs that started on this release are still executing. |
| `RELEASE_DRAIN_STATE_DRAINED` | 2 | DRAINED: none are. The cluster refreshes this on a delay of minutes; drain_checked_at says when it last looked. |

### ReleaseRole

ReleaseRole is what a release does with NEW runs. It never describes runs
already executing: those finish on the release that started them.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RELEASE_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `RELEASE_ROLE_CURRENT` | 1 | CURRENT takes every new run that is not sent to a ramping release. |
| `RELEASE_ROLE_RAMPING` | 2 | RAMPING takes ramp_percent of new runs. |
| `RELEASE_ROLE_PREVIOUS` | 3 | PREVIOUS took new runs once and takes none now. It may still be finishing some; drain_state says whether it is. |
| `RELEASE_ROLE_CANDIDATE` | 4 | CANDIDATE has registered — at least one of its processes polled with ORK_BUILD_ID set — and has never taken new runs. |

### RetryState

RetryState is why Temporal stopped retrying a task. It mirrors
temporal.api.enums.v1.RetryState with its own numbering, because a value of
another proto package's enum may not be carried by number: the mapping is
explicit, in internal/engine/workflow.go.

temporal's RETRY_STATE_IN_PROGRESS has no member here on purpose. It names a
retry that has not finished, and this field is only ever set from the error
of a task that already reached a terminal outcome; it maps to UNSPECIFIED.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RETRY_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `RETRY_STATE_NON_RETRYABLE_FAILURE` | 1 |  |
| `RETRY_STATE_TIMEOUT` | 2 |  |
| `RETRY_STATE_MAXIMUM_ATTEMPTS_REACHED` | 3 |  |
| `RETRY_STATE_RETRY_POLICY_NOT_SET` | 4 |  |
| `RETRY_STATE_CANCEL_REQUESTED` | 5 |  |
| `RETRY_STATE_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | 6 |  |

### RunOriginKind

RunOriginKind is WHAT started a run. It is decided by the process that
accepted the submission and is never accepted from a client: the public
SubmitRun RPC produces SUBMIT, or RUN_AGAIN when the request names a
source run the server confirms exists; the trigger door produces TRIGGER
from its stored record; schedule and composition code produce SCHEDULE
and PARENT_RUN. A caller who could claim "trigger" would be claiming an
audit fact, so no request field carries a kind.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RUN_ORIGIN_KIND_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | UNSPECIFIED is what a run recorded before origins existed carries. Every client renders it as "unrecorded" — never as SUBMIT, because "a person submitted this" is a claim, and no evidence supports it. |
| `RUN_ORIGIN_KIND_SUBMIT` | 1 | SUBMIT: SubmitRun over Connect — orkctl run submit, the UI's submit dialog, or a direct API call. id is empty. |
| `RUN_ORIGIN_KIND_TRIGGER` | 2 | TRIGGER: POST /v1/triggers/{id}. id is the trigger id (trg-…). |
| `RUN_ORIGIN_KIND_SCHEDULE` | 3 | SCHEDULE: a schedule fired. id is the schedule id (sch-…). Defined here so orkflow-schedules stamps it without touching Run; nothing produces it until that proposal lands. |
| `RUN_ORIGIN_KIND_PARENT_RUN` | 4 | PARENT_RUN: a child run started by a composing parent. id is the PARENT run's id. Defined here so composed-orkflows adds no Run field of its own; nothing produces it until that proposal lands. |
| `RUN_ORIGIN_KIND_RUN_AGAIN` | 5 | RUN_AGAIN: `orkctl run again` or the run page's Run again. id is the SOURCE run's id, which the server confirmed exists in this namespace. |

Status is the lifecycle state shared by runs and task runs.

| Value | Number | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `STATUS_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 |  |
| `STATUS_PENDING` | 1 |  |
| `STATUS_RUNNING` | 2 |  |
| `STATUS_SUCCEEDED` | 3 |  |

| `STATUS_CANCELED` | 5 |  |

| `STATUS_AWAITING` | 7 | AWAITING is a TASK status only, like SKIPPED: the task is waiting to be resolved from outside the run. A run with an awaiting task is RUNNING. |

| `TASK_LOG_EXPORT_ENABLED` | 1 |  |
| `TASK_LOG_EXPORT_DISABLED` | 2 |  |
